* **Touch delay removed + RTC (user: "start by removing the touch delay, then check the clock and RTC", 2026-10-29).** The delay was only a safety margin (sweet_touch.c: "if the bus access below hangs the SoC, the persistent log and the GUI got there first"; default 45, our images had 90). xnu **3003** (`3003-dipper-rtc-diagnostics.patch`, commit 11e135c, fork CI run 40910677200 success, 3001-3003 applied, kernel sha256 6f251fa01eb5c2ca... -> `xnu/out-dipper-40910677200/`): sr_raw() records the failing step, sr_explain() prints it once ("SWEET RTC: no wall clock: ..." at boot, "SWEET RTC: time not kept: ..." when iOS sets the time) with the RTC APID/owner/RTC_CTRL; no new register access. Image `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-8-wlan.img` (sha256 b873acff6e38c0b3...): ios26-7-wlan's args with `sweettouchdelay=0` (the only difference). **Boot 8 (17:45:12, log research/dipper-ios26-8-wlan.log):** touch worked with no delay (its start lines now fall before the UDP log's 64 KiB replay: the touch thread starts at kernel init, not at backboardd's open); Wi-Fi joined the user's iPhone hotspot (WPA2-PSK, `keys -> CONNECTED (252 ms)`); **`SWEET RTC: offset 0 -> 1761313336 (raw 31979157, time 1793292493)`** (= 2026-10-29 16:48:13 UTC, no FAILED): the RTC path WORKS on the Mi 8. The 1969 clock was only "no offset stored yet": the PMIC RTC counts raw seconds since its own reset (31979157 s = 370 days), the offset is kept in the RTC alarm data registers (alarm disabled), and no boot before had network time (no Wi-Fi) to set it. The boot's `SWEET RTC: raw ... -> ...` line is printed at clock init, before the UDP replay window, which is why no log had a SWEET RTC line. The offset lives in the PMIC, so userdata reflashes keep it; Android (if restored) may reuse the RTC alarm and clobber it. Expect the next boot to start at the right time. Log 8 ends at ~17:51 (up_s 3625) with no panic/reboot line; the phone was later found in Bergamota fastboot (unclean end assumed) -> delta reflash: `963 MiB of 24576 MiB` differed, `RESULT OK FLASHED userdata: 3 MiB sent (delta) and verified in 501 s`; phone in Bergamota fastboot, pristine root.

* **🎉 BO HANDLE LEAK FOUND AND FIXED (2026-10-29 ~23:45-23:58).** Boot 14 soft-rebooted after the user's UI use; its buffer log (research/chl-work/boot14/drmlog/backboardd-65.log, 24 MB, 224 s) shows backboardd's live handles 62 at 54 s -> 4094 at 216 s (~25/s net while the UI animates), 3240 of the 4094 unused by any submit in the last 30 s; live set: 2695 x 20480 B (12925 of that size closed), 989 x 36864 B, 181 x 69632 B; **2123 of the live 20480-byte BOs were never in any submit.** Cause in Chlorophyll `air/chl_vk.c`: texture uploads (`chl_texture_replace`, bgmtl.m's per-frame "linear texture refresh"/surface copies) record into a prologue command buffer (`pro_begin`, a fresh vkAllocateCommandBuffers each time), `pro_submit_locked` parks it in `pro_inflight[]`, and `pro_reap` released its held objects and destroyed its fence but never freed the command buffer, so every prologue leaked its Turnip command-stream BOs (16/32 KiB + Chlorophyll's 4 KiB slack page = 20480/36864); `vkFreeCommandBuffers` was not even in the CHL_DEVICE_FNS table. **Fix:** gpu/metal commit **0523583** (local branch `dipper` of the Chlorophyll submodule: upstream ry-diffusion/Chlorophyll cannot be pushed from here, so the gitlink is NOT bumped; the same change is `gpu/chlorophyll-patches/0001-chl-free-each-prologue-command-buffer.patch`): `vkFreeCommandBuffers(d->dev, d->pro_pool, 1, &pro_inflight[i].cb)` in pro_reap (pro_lock held by both callers, which also serialises the pool). Rebuilt (build-turnip.sh incremental + build-metal.sh): libchlorophyll.dylib sha256 2e2faea3bf0d8b81... RPMh BCM votes as Linux's bcm-voter computes them: MC0 unit 2000000 width 16 (7216 -> y 14432), SH0 unit 4000000 width 64 (twice DDR, y 14432), SH5 width 32 (y 3608); MC0 alone: 64 MB reads 267 -> 186 ns, memcpy 7.1 -> 9.2 GB/s. * **GLASS ICONS FIXED, ICONSERVICESAGENT BACK ON THE GPU (user 2026-10-31: "Yes, go ahead" to why the GPU damages glass icons). gpu/metal f31fcbd, inject ebfaff8a161b, libchlorophyll unchanged (2f1a7a5dadb6). No kernel change, no CI run. The kill switch and `tools/dipper-settings-icons.sh` are gone.** **Cause, observed:** RenderBox draws each layer of an icon into its own RGBA16F IOSurface, then wraps the surface in a second MTLTexture to sample it. A surface Turnip refuses to import was `_surfCopy`: own memory, filled from the surface at each use, never written back ("good for sampling, which is all CA does with those"). So the layer was drawn and then read as empty. New switch `chl.passdump` showed it: Notes' yellow band is right in surface 1205 (608x153), every later pass sampling it gets nothing. Refused: pitch not 128-aligned (fd6_layout.c; IOSurface aligns to 64: 3392, 960, 2240), or the image's height aligned to 4 rows exceeds the surface (608x153: 753664 bytes, 758784 asked; `real_size < size`). So which layers die depends on their size: the same icons each time, and `TU_DEBUG=sysmem`, `gmem`, `flushall` gave pixel-identical damage. It also explains the blank 40x40 from `iconq`. **Fix:** `bgCopyWriteBack` at completion, `bg_surfwb_wait` for a reader of a surface in flight (at most 500 ms). **A second bug appeared once layers existed, and it is avoided, not understood:** icons over about 220 px (several tiles; my test size 528) give an SMMU fault, TP|VFD, always in the agent: FAR 0x2504c00, 0x2504000, 0x24d7080, 0x247cd80. (4b) data: ASM stream (open write, PCM 48 kHz 16-bit) + ADM COPP on the port + ADM_CMD_MATRIX_MAP_ROUTINGS, PCM buffers in memory the DSP reaches: ASM_CMD_SHARED_MEM_MAP_REGIONS with physical addresses; the DSP's SMMU stream for audio (mainline sdm845 `q6asmdai` iommus = <&apps_smmu 0x1821 0x0>) must be mapped/bypassed (`sweet_smmu_map_sid()` exists for the WLAN stream 0x40). Mac-microphone tone check here (user's terminal microphone permission, phone next to the Mac). (6) iOS audio device: a kernel IOAudio2-style device or a HAL plug-in in place of the null device, feeding (4b).

Asserted in wlan_vdev.c:_wlan_vdev_down:3440`, Wi-Fi gone until a reboot, the rest of iOS unaffected. There is still no modem restart: any other firmware assert has the same effect. **3036:** (1) **PEER_DELETE, wait for PEER_UNMAP, then VDEV_DOWN and VDEV_STOP.** `ST_DOWN` did VDEV_DOWN first. Upstream (read, `ieee80211_set_disassoc`, `ath10k_sta_state`, `ath10k_bss_disassoc`, `unassign_vif_chanctx`): `sta_info_flush` before BSS_CHANGED_ASSOC, vdev stop last. No upstream comment says why. A kernel with only this change: 4 of 4 clean, so this was the cause; the earlier "clean teardown" of boot 53 on the Poco F1 was before VDEV_UP, so it never sent the command that asserts. (2) **`sta_step` took `in` before the leave was handled,** so the first pass of `ST_DOWN` saw the time in the old state and every wait ran out: the deauthentication was discarded (`management TX done: NOT acked (status 1)`), the AP was never told. Now acked (status 0). (3) As upstream, now that the path runs: power save off before the deauthentication, mode 1 after VDEV_STOP. **Tested, forced with `/var/root/sweetwifi disassoc` (new command):** 6 of 6 and image 57 4 of 4, half of them during a transfer, rejoin by wifid in 8-12 s, deauthentication acked. During a transfer the AP answers `deauthentication from the AP, reason 7`: data still reaching it after our deauthentication; harmless. As if the AP kicked us (throwaway `sta.by_ap = true`, no deauthentication sent): 4 of 4, 9-12 s. Image 57: 0 modem crashes in 5 joins, 60 pings in 10 min 0 lost, 45.3/63.3 Mbit/s, 0 recoveries, 0 hangs. **Not tested:** a real AP going away (a router restart: the user's call), or walking out of range; `PEER_STA_KICKOUT` takes the same teardown by reading the code. **To watch for:** `wlan_powersave_sta.c:wlan_ps_sta_health_monitor_timeout:2437` (`dipper-ios26-7-wlan.log`, right after joining an open network, power save off, not seen since).

Not every request takes that path. **Decision:** not fixable by repairing something here. Mescal and Anisette prove to Apple that this is a genuine activated iPhone; making them pass would mean forging that identity, which I will not do, and a stub would be refused by the server anyway. Why fairplayd.H2 exits is still a guess (no FairPlay hardware). Other apps that call Apple's signed services will likely fail the same way (inference). Widgets' "Weather Unavailable" is this too.
* **THE SPEAKER PLAYER IN THE KERNEL, xnu 3045 (user 2026-11-04: "yeah build it"; research tree a6d423d, local only like the earlier ones, `xnu/patches-12377/3045-dipper-audio-player.patch`, kernel `xnu/out-dipper-local-3040/kernel.development.sweet.3045` sha256 d2de8af86d6e95a4..., image `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-69-player.img` = sweetaudio=3; parent commit e56a8b1).** `bsd/dev/dipper_audio.c` now does in the kernel what `dipper-speaker.sh tone` did by hand: `kern.sweet_audio_play` (u32 op: 1 start, 2 stop, 3 + PCM appended to the ring, EAGAIN while it does not fit, 4 drain; reads back `struct pl_status`) and `kern.sweet_audio_amp` (u8 1 on / 0 off + an I2C script; the amp's scripts stay in user space because they carry TI's firmware). Start, in the audio thread: SMMU SID 0x1821, pins, LPASS bit clock, I2S config, DEVICE_START, amp on script, ASM mem map of the whole window, open write, ADM COPP open (port 0x1006), matrix routing, media format, RUN; then 4 writes of one 20 ms period (3840 B) stay queued in the DSP and each `ASM_DATA_EVENT_WRITE_DONE_V2` (handled quietly, no log line) sends the next; with no data in the ring (5.46 s, 273 periods, at window offset 0) it sends a period of zeros from right after the ring, so the stream never starves. Stop/drain/stall (no WRITE_DONE for 1 s): amp off script + amp reset low, ASM pause + close, **ADM close (q6adm.c adm_close: src port = AFE port 0x1006, dest port = the COPP id; status 0 now, so COPP 0 is reused)**, unmap, DEVICE_STOP, clock off, pins back, one summary line. While playing with the amp scripted, the amp's FLAGS_1/FLAGS_2 are read every second (book 0 page 0 set first) and TI's critical masks (FLAGS_1 & 0xfc, FLAGS_2 & 0x0c) or an I2C error stop everything. The thread polls GLINK every 2 ms while playing (20 ms idle). New `tools/sweetnet/sweetplay.c` (`sweetplay [-a AMP_ON] [-o AMP_OFF] FILE|-`, `-s` state, `-x` stop), `dipper-speaker.sh play FILE` (amp-on.bin = load-rom.bin + on-g2.bin, gain 2), `mkpcm.py` writes any length. **Boot 69 on the old root, amp NOT scripted (silent), observed:** 20 s 440 Hz file (3.84 MB, about 3.7 laps of the ring): 20.00 s of audio in 20.10 s, 1005 writes, 5 periods of zeros (the 4 queued at start + 1, all before the data), **0 after the data started, 0 errors, 0 waits for room**, every teardown status 0. Second run stopped by `sweetplay -x` after 4 s: 791040 B played, all statuses 0, the client got EPIPE as designed. **HEARD THROUGH THE PLAYER, boot 69c on the re-flashed root, 2026-11-04 ~13:33 CET (user listening, `sp.sh play /var/root/amp/scale.pcm`: 16 notes C4-C5-C4, 1 s each, -30 dBFS, 30 ms fades, amp ROM mode gain 2): user: "Clean scale, 16 notes" (no clicks, dropouts or stutter).** Observed on the phone: amp on 125 ops error 0 (safe guard 0x5a, POWER_CTRL 0xf8/0xa3, SPK_CTRL 0x14), started in 0.51 s, 16.00 s of audio in 16.14 s, 804 writes, 4 periods of zeros all before the data (0 after), 0 errors, 0 waits for room, 16 amp checks all FLAGS_1 0x02 / FLAGS_2 0x00, amp off 20 ops error 0, every teardown status 0, COPP 0 again. **Next:** (6) an iOS audio device feeding the ring (the WRITE_DONEs give the clock: played bytes / 192000 s), software volume, and the tuning program with speaker protection before anything louder. * **MICROPHONE + EARPIECE, STARTED 2026-11-05 ~22:40 (user: "no sim inside at the moment, let's fix microphone and earpiece first").** **Facts (observed: live DT `dtb/dipper/live.dtb`, `backup/dipper/vendor.img` /etc/mixer_paths_tavil.xml + audio_platform_info.xml + /lib/hw/audio.primary.sdm845.so, Lineage `dipper-audio-overlay.dtsi`):** the microphones are on the **WCD9340 (Tavil) codec**: Xiaomi's `handset-mic` = path `dmic3` (CDC_IF TX7 <- DEC7 <- ADC MUX7 DMIC <- DMIC MUX7 DMIC2, SLIM TX7 into AIF1_CAP, SLIM_0_TX one channel), `speaker-mic` = `dmic2` (DMIC1), `main-mic` = AMIC ADC3 on DEC5, `handset-dmic-dual-adc` = AMIC ADC1..4; DT micbias1/3/4 2700 mV, micbias2 1800 mV, `qcom,cdc-dmic-sample-rate`, `qcom,adc2-switch-gpio`. Tavil: `qcom,tavil-slim-pgd` under `slim@171c0000` (`qcom,slim-ngd`, cell-index 1, regs 0x171c0000+0x2c000 and BAM 0x17184000+0x2a000, IRQs SPI 163/164, `qcom,ea-pc` 0x270, `qcom,apps-ch-pipes` 0x780000), PGD elemental address 00 01 50 02 17 02, IFD 00 00 50 02 17 02, MCLK 9.6 MHz (`wcd_clk`), all five supplies one 1.8 V rail, reset via `cdc_reset_ctrl`, IRQs through `wcd9xxx_intr`. The ADSP is the SLIMbus manager (ngd = apps is a non-ported device) and already announces QMI service 0x301 (SLIMbus) on the QRTR link the audio code serves (xnu 3042). **Earpiece: not settled.** Xiaomi's `handset` device path is the generic Qualcomm one (RX0 -> RX INT7 -> COMP7 -> `SpkrLeft` SoundWire WSA, `EAR SPKR PA Gain`), but `wsa-max-devs = 0`; `handset-qrd` = RX INT0 -> EAR PA; the `... receiver` use-case paths and `voicemmode1-call receiver` route to QUAT_MI2S_RX (the TAS2557 port), yet the TAS2557 node has no switch and the HAL has no `receiver` device name. Most likely (guess) the earpiece is on Tavil's EAR output, to be confirmed by ear. **Reference needed:** this Lineage tree has only `wcd9xxx-core*.c`, `audio-ext-clk*.c` and `wcd934x_registers.h` (no SLIMbus controller, no wcd934x codec driver); mainline Linux has `drivers/slimbus/qcom-ngd-ctrl.c`, `sound/soc/codecs/wcd934x.c`, `drivers/mfd/wcd934x.c` (SDM845: Poco F1, Pixel 3). **Plan (mine):** (1) SLIMbus NGD on the apps side + the ADSP's SLIMbus QMI (power up), codec reset + MCLK through the AFE clock code, enumerate the codec and read its chip id = "the codec answers"; (2) Tavil init (clocks, bias, defaults); (3) microphone: DMIC2 -> DEC7 -> SLIM TX7, AFE SLIMBUS_0_TX port, a level meter in a sysctl (user speaks/taps), then an iOS input stream in SweetSpeaker.driver; (4) earpiece: SLIMBUS_0_RX -> RX0 -> INT0 -> EAR PA (or INT7), test tone at very low level with the user listening, then a Receiver output in iOS; (5) calls later use the same paths (voice sessions). Scale (guess): days. **Sources (user OK to download, 2026-11-05 ~22:50):** the Lineage tree `research/lineage-sdm845` is a blobless sparse checkout of LineageOS/android_kernel_xiaomi_sdm845, so the codec/SLIMbus folders were simply not checked out; added: `techpack/audio/asoc/codecs/wcd934x/` (Qualcomm's downstream Tavil driver, the one Android ran, same control names as Xiaomi's mixer file), `drivers/slimbus/` (slim-msm-ngd.c, slim-msm.c, slimbus.c), `include/linux/slimbus/`, `techpack/audio/soc/` (SoundWire, pinctrl-wcd). Mainline copies (torvalds/linux master d68ce4e71248, gitignored) in `research/mainline-ref/`: qcom-ngd-ctrl.c, sound/soc/codecs/wcd934x.c, mfd/wcd934x.c, wcd934x registers.h. Register facts only, no code copied. **Step 1 recipe (from slim-msm-ngd.c / slim-msm.c / slim-msm.h, not run yet):** QMI to the ADSP's SLIMbus service 0x301 instance 0: SELECT_INSTANCE 0x20 {TLV 0x01 u32 instance = ctrl nr >> 1 = 0 (cell-index 1), TLV 0x10 u32 mode 1 = satellite}, then POWER 0x21 {TLV 0x01 u32 2 = active}; (CHECK_FRAMER_STATUS 0x22). Controller version = readl(base 0x171c0000) >> 16 (non-zero -> V2), NGD block at base + 0x1000 (V2, odd nr): CFG 0x0 (bit0 enable, bit1 RX msgq, bit2 TX msgq: we use neither = register FIFOs), STATUS 0x4 (bit1 = has a logical address), RX_MSGQ_CFG 0x8 (|= 0x10000 timeout), INT_EN 0x10 / INT_STAT 0x14 / INT_CLR 0x18 (bit31 TX sent, 30 RX received, 29 dev err, 28 IE/VE change, 27 TX invalid, 26 msg buf contention, 25 TX nacked, 24 reconfig done), TX_MSG 0x30.., RX_MSG 0x70.. (first word: len = bits 0-4, mt = bits 5-7, mc = byte 1; first word assembled as len | mt<<5 | mc<<8 | dt<<15 | la<<16). Sequence: INT_EN = 0xBE000000 | (as Linux: nacked, conte, tx inval, ie/ve, dev err, tx sent), RX timeout, CFG = 1; the manager then sends MASTER_CAPABILITY (mt 6 src-referred user, mc 0x00); answer REPORT_SATELLITE (mc 0x01, to LA 0xFF, payload D9 C5 01 01), wait GENERIC_ACK (mc 0x25, payload bit 0x20 = success); then ADDR_QUERY (mc 0x0D, EA 00 01 50 02 17 02) -> ADDR_REPLY (mc 0x0E: EA + LA at byte 10); codec registers then through REQUEST_VALUE 0x60 / REPLY_VALUE 0x64 (tid at byte 3) to that LA. Before that the codec needs its reset GPIO released, the 1.8 V rail and MCLK 9.6 MHz (correction: the DT's wcd_clk is audio_ext_clk_lnbb = RPMh LN_BB_CLK2 "lnbclka2", not an AFE clock; reset = TLMM 64 NORTH; supply pm8998 s4 stub).

Rolling back would keep the shared blocks (the next journal write would overwrite the dyld cache on disk), so: **fixed copy** `research/fsck/userdata-hfs-20261106-fixed.img` = the repaired volume + the 221 reference pages written at the physical offsets macOS reports for those pages (F_LOG2PHYS_EXT on a read-only mount); verified: fsck_hfs -fn OK, both files hash equal to the reference, the Cryptex path is the same inode; it differs from the phone's current content in 15 x 64 KiB blocks (0.9 MiB). Write-back waits for the user's OK; the phone needs a forced restart into Bergamota fastboot first. Lesson: after an fsck repair, diff the files (not only the volume) against the pre-repair copy before writing it back. **Fix written (user: "it is already there" = in Bergamota fastboot), 01:16-01:25: `DELTA 1048576` (16 blocks: the 15 counted + most likely the volume header the failed boot touched), `RESULT OK FLASHED userdata: 1 MiB sent (delta) and verified in 501 s`. * **SENSORS, STARTED 2026-11-06 ~12:40 (task from the main session: rotation / CoreMotion, auto-brightness, proximity at the ear, compass).** **How to test (the user asked: an IPA test app, or our own suite?):** bring-up with command-line probes over SSH, as for audio and the modem: `sweetsys kern.sweet_ssc=N` now, later a `tools/sweetnet` tool that lists the SLPI's sensors and prints live samples (tilt the phone, cover the top, shine a light). They log to the UDP console and need no UI. Once iOS sees a sensor, the stock apps are the hands-on test: screen rotation, Compass, Measure's Level, Settings > Display > Auto-Brightness, the screen going off at the ear during a receiver-route session (`sweetaqin ... -e`). An IPA dashboard (TrollStore is in the root) is optional, for later.
  **Hardware (observed, nothing booted):** no sensor is on an AP bus: the live DT has only `qcom,msm-ssc-sensors` (firmware-name `slpi_dp`) and the SLPI PIL node; the one apps-side "sensor" chip is the BCM4775 GNSS. The phone's own sensor registry (backup/dipper/persist.img `sensors/registry/registry/*`, written by Android; `sensors/sensors_list.txt` of 2020-04-26) and `/vendor/etc/sensors/config/sdm845_*.json` (backup/dipper/vendor.img, read with Homebrew e2fsprogs `debugfs`): **TDK ICM-206xx** (`icm206xx_0`; its OIS accel/gyro streams suggest the ICM-20690, not confirmed) accel + gyro on SSC SPI (bus_instance 2, CS 0, 3.3 MHz, IRQ 118, orient x,-y,-z, also OIS accel/gyro streams); **AKM AK0991x** magnetometer (`ak0991x_0`, I2C bus 1 address 0x0c, IRQ 119, orient +x,-y,-z, factory calibration matrix in the registry); **AMS TMD2725** ALS + proximity (`tmd2725`, I2C bus 1 0x39, IRQ 120, rails sensor_vdd + sensor_vddio, als/prox factory calibration in the registry); **ADI ADUX1050** capacitive proximity (I2C bus 1 0x2c, the SAME IRQ 120: one of the two is a board alternative; which one is fitted is NOT known); **Bosch BMP285** pressure + temperature (I2C bus 1 0x77). Android's list: ambient_light, proximity, pressure, sensor_temperature, accel, gyro, mag, plus fused/virtual ones (gravity, game_rv, geomag_rv, device_orient, pedometer, sig_motion, tilt, pickup, ...) computed on the SLPI. Persist also holds `acc_caldata.txt` / `gyro_caldata.txt`. The buses are on the SSC's OWN 18-pin TLMM (registry `power.gpio.gpio_0..17`, function selects 1/2) and the rails are PMIC clients the SLPI votes itself (`/pmic/client/sensor_vdd`, `sensor_vddio`): no AP-side shortcut like the touch driver's bit-banged I2C (not tried; the pins are not the AP TLMM's). There is also an Elliptic Labs ultrasound proximity path: the vendor audio HAL has `ultrasound_*` hooks (`ultrasound_apply_fusion_sensor_path`), `/vendor/etc/mixer_paths_tavil.xml` has a path `ultrasound-proximity` and "Ultrasound Enable/Mode/Rx Port" controls, and the shared Xiaomi SDM845 kernel builds `techpack/audio/asoc/elliptic/` + `apr_elliptic.c` (on the audio DSP); whether the Mi 8 takes call proximity from it, from the TMD2725, or fuses both is not known.
  **SLPI facts (live DT + firmware, observed):** `qcom,ssc@5c00000` pil-tz-generic, PAS id 12, SMEM crash item 424, signal-aop, vdd_cx = `lcx.lvl`, vdd_mx = `lmx.lvl` (RPMh ARC, level 0x181, keep-proxy-regs-on), carve-out `pil_slpi_region` 0x96b00000 + 0x1400000 (no-map, low DDR bank, outside the kernel's `--highmem` RAM; ADSP's is 0x8c500000); smp2p-dsps remote pid 3, doorbell 0x1799000c bit 26, IRQ 172 (SMEM items 481 in / 430 out: Xiaomi's `include/soc/qcom/smem.h` SMEM_SMP2P_SENSOR_BASE 481 + apps pid 0, SMEM_SMP2P_APPS_BASE 427 + pid 3; crash reason 424 = SMEM_SSR_REASON_DSPS0); GLINK SMEM edge `dsps` (doorbell bit 24, IRQ 170). Linux (Lineage `drivers/sensors/sensors_ssc.c`): `subsystem_get_with_fwname("slpi", "slpi_dp")`. Modem partition `/image`: `SLPI_DP.MDT` + `B00..B23` (no B20; 25 phdrs, relocatable, 0x1300000 bytes: fits), also SLPI / SLPI_BR / SLPI_PS / SLPI_US for other Xiaomi boards, and `SLPIR.JSN` / `SLPIUS.JSN` = pd-mapper domains `msm/slpi/root_pd` and `msm/slpi/sensor_pd` (tms/servreg, instance 90). The `dsp` partition (`/sdsp`) holds the SLPI's FastRPC side: `fastrpc_shell_2`, CHRE skels, `map_SSC_SLPI_USER_*.txt`. Vendor userspace: `sscrpcd` + `libsns_registry_skel.so` (serves the registry files to the SLPI over FastRPC), `libssc.so` / `sensors.ssc.so` (the QMI client), `/vendor/etc/sensors/sns_reg_config` (registry output `/mnt/vendor/persist/sensors/registry/registry`).
  **Linux reference (read, not run):** postmarketOS on SDM845 (OnePlus 6, Poco F1) reads these sensors with hexagonrpcd (serves the registry/config files to the SLPI over FastRPC) and libssc (QMI service 400 = SNS client, protobuf payloads: SUID lookup by data type "accel", "gyro", "mag", "ambient_light", "proximity", then a stream request), see `docs/FORKS_SURVEY.md` G4. Whether this SLPI build starts its sensors WITHOUT the AP serving the registry is reported (postmarketOS) as no, not checked here.
  **How iOS 26.6.2 wants them (observed in binaries from the phone and the DSC; nothing tried):** iPhone 11 has its sensors behind the AOP; the n104 ADT has `/arm-io/aop/iop-aop-nub/{accel,gyro,compass,pressure,prox,spherecontrol,SPUApp}` with `device-usage-page`/`device-usage` = accel 0xff00/3, gyro 0xff00/9, compass 0xff00/10 (kHIDPage_AppleVendor), prox 0xff00/8, pressure 0x20/0x31 (HID sensor page, barometer), calibration from syscfg; no `als` node there. Consumers: **locationd** (CoreMotion's daemon, /usr/libexec/locationd) matches HID services by `PrimaryUsagePage`/`PrimaryUsage`/`DeviceUsagePairs`, sets `ReportInterval`/`BatchInterval`, has a high-rate "FastPath" (`AppleSPUHIDDevice` / `AppleSPUFastpathDriver` / `AppleSPUFastpathInterface`, CLIoHidFastPathDevice.mm) and logs "Accel unavailable, unable to establish hid interface" and "No accelerometer; not detecting orientation!". **backboardd** takes device orientation from CoreMotion (`CMDeviceOrientationManager startDeviceOrientationUpdatesToQueue:`), i.e. from locationd's accelerometer: screen rotation needs locationd to see an accelerometer; proximity it matches itself (BKIOHIDServiceMatcher, BKHIDProximityEventProcessor, `setProximityDetectionMode:`, BKSProximitySensor IPC: VirtualAudio's ReceiverProximityIODelegate goes through this); auto-brightness is CoreBrightness inside backboardd (`CBALSService`, matches by PrimaryUsagePage/PrimaryUsage, "new ALS service added", also reads `IODeviceTree:/arm-io/aop/iop-aop-nub/als` and `als-supports-color`). Our kernel already serves iOS HID event services (`iokit/Kernel/arm/hid/SweetHID.cpp`: SweetHIDButtons, SweetHIDTouch, Transport "SPU", `hidutil list` shows them) and its IOHIDEvent has accelerometerEvent, gyroEvent, compassEvent, ambientLightSensorEvent, proximityEvent, atmosphericPressureEvent: the iOS side is new SweetHID services with the iPhone's usage pairs, the way VirtualAudio wanted its devices by UID.
  **Plan:** **S1** SLPI up (kernel, new `bsd/dev/dipper_sensors.c`, sysctl `kern.sweet_ssc`): 1 probe, 2 boot (QMP, lcx/lmx, SMP2P, PAS 12), then GLINK on the `dsps` edge + QRTR (the audio code's GLINK/QRTR, second edge) to list the SLPI's services and answer its pd-mapper queries from the JSN files. **S2** registry: if no sensors appear, a FastRPC responder on GLINK `fastrpcglink-apps-dsp` (dsps) that serves the registry/config files (hexagonrpcd's apps_std file calls), from a copy of /vendor/etc/sensors/config + persist/sensors/registry on the iOS root (device calibration: never in git). **S3** QMI SNS client (service 400, protobuf): kernel pass-through like `kern.sweet_qmi` (3057) + a `tools/sweetnet` probe (list SUIDs, stream accel/gyro/mag/ALS/prox) to iterate without kernel rebuilds. **S4** iOS: SweetHID accel/gyro/compass/ALS/prox/pressure services with the n104 usage pairs, fed from S3; ReportInterval/BatchInterval through setProperties; maybe the ADT's aop sensor nodes. CoreMotion's CMDeviceOrientationManager runs inside backboardd and, on this hardware class, asks the AOP for the orientation through AppleSPU's HID driver interface (CLSPUHIDDriverInterface), which the Mi 8 does not have. Chlorophyll could not import a surface in that shape, made it a plain copy (bgmtl trace: `surface copy refresh: 3328 bytes per row for a region whose rows need 7168`) and in the compositor never wrote copies back, so the panel kept the last portrait frame until the app turned back (trace of backboardd: 117 passes into `1792x828 ... surface 949`, none into 828x1792). `CA_DISABLE_DISPLAY_ROTATION=1` (bgmtl-bb.env) changed nothing; QuartzCore reads `IOMFBSupportsRotation` / `SupportsRotation` from the framebuffer, which our AppleCLCD does not publish. **Fix (gpu/metal src/bgmtl.m):** a rotated IOSurface texture gets its own memory in the rotated shape plus an unrotated twin over the same surface (imported); at every commit that drew into it, one full-screen triangle (MSL compiled in the process, like the MPS blur) copies it turned into the twin, i.e. the panel's surface. When the surface was drawn some other way since (portrait in between), the rotated texture is first filled from the surface on the CPU (once per turn per framebuffer). TEST image 130d (sha256 59a5fadae85812db..., kernel e1dcff09989bb51a..., `xnu/out-dipper-local-3085/kernel.development.sweet.3085d`), RAM-booted 18:02: Camera open, shutter at 18:03: `still buffer: 16 MiB of pages at IOVA 0x41000000`, `still: mode 0 half rate, sequence 100 records (0 NAK), settle 16, exposure 1554 lines (fll 3140) again 480 dgain 0x200, stream on` and **nothing after it**; ping dead from then on, not in fastboot, the Mac's USB interface still active. So it stops within the first mode 0 frame (frame 0's wait is 400 ms and nothing after it was logged), with the page-mapped buffer and HUPCF: not the 2 MiB block mapping, not an SMMU fault blocking USB (guesses ruled out, not proven by a fault line). The only working run of this path is the 16:12 root test with Camera closed. Differences while Camera runs (guesses): GPU and display traffic, CPU load, sweetcam's live reads. **The user, asked before the second power-button restart: "Screen frozen"** (so a whole-phone freeze, not only USB). **ROOT CAUSE FOUND (18:15-18:35) and FIXED:** TEST image 130e (3085e: the preview buffers page-mapped too, `sweet_smmu_map32_pages`, so a frame running past one faults at its end instead of overwriting kernel memory; write master state logged at each step; sha256 7469c902530dcca7..., kernel 954e39e8b55bed92...): photo 1 worked (frame 0 at the still buffer 0x40c00000), photo 2 (three tries) logged `frame 0 done: WM0 status 0x40800000` and `frame 0 NOT in the still buffer (... mode 2 guards changed 4088 ...; SMMU FSR 0x80000402 FAR 0x40abc000)`: frame 0 went into preview buffer 2 and faulted exactly at its mapped end, the phone stayed up. Observed rule (from the logs, not a document): the IFE write master QUEUES image addresses; each frame start takes the oldest written one and WM0 STATUS0 (0x2200) then reads it; the stream loop writes the next preview buffer's address after every frame done. When the sensor stopped in the vertical blank, that preview address was still queued and mode 0's first frame took it (15 MB into a 2.8 MB buffer, mapped by 2 MiB blocks until 3085e: kernel memory overwritten = the freezes at 16:16 and 18:03 and the pink photos); when a mode 2 frame had already started, it took that address and the still worked (the 16:12 root test, 130e photo 1). **xnu 3085f** (in 3086, tree 5eebdc6): when a still is asked, the stream loop queues the still buffer's address instead of the next preview buffer's and only then calls c4_still; c4_still reads STATUS0 to know whether a mode 2 frame took it (queue it again) or not; after the last mode 0 frame it queues a sink B (the still buffer is now 2 x 16 MiB: A the frame, B the sink) and counts the frames after it; if none took B the next frame after the still lands in B and the loop does not publish it (`st_phantom`); the sysctl makes the still buffer before the request; a timeout after frame 0 now fails the still (no partial ones); `s0_halt` takes frame count 0xff (standby) as stopped. **TEST image 130f** `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-130f-still.img` (sha256 1d3d80b191279993..., kernel 5b165e980e7754b1..., `xnu/out-dipper-local-3085/kernel.development.sweet.3085f`), RAM-booted 18:31: **six Camera photos in a row (18:32-18:35), every one `armed for mode 0 (address queued by the loop)` (the case that froze before), frame 0 at 0x40c00000, `4 frames (+1 after the last)`, pieces written 8 of 8, guard untouched, mode 2 guards changed 0, no SMMU fault, back to mode 2; the phone stayed up and the preview ran on** (screenshot). Photos IMG_0017-0022: 1924x1444 JPEG, about 850 KB (the preview-based ones 380-580 KB), the whole 4:3 sensor field (about 1.4x wider than the preview's 4:3 crop of the 16:9 frame), right colours; grainy in the dim room (analog gain 16). sweetcam's own `still:` lines did not reach `sweetlog` (other cameracaptured lines did; not looked into), so that it developed them per 2x2 cell is inferred from the field of view and the kernel's log, not seen. Not done: the flashlight/jetsam cycle (above); a quality comparison against the preview-based stills on the same scene; 130f is a test image (the default is still 129).
* **THE CAMERA'S RESTART CYCLE AT IDLE FIXED (2026-11-09 18:43-18:58, user: "Yes, fix it").** The cycle (found in step 3): at every cameracaptured launch SpringBoard's flashlight client (`FigFlashlightCreate ... clientType: AVFlashlight`) has the default camera device made and its streams requested (no Start); sweetcam started the sensor at RequestStreams (HakiOS's way), so the sensor ran ~135 frames for the device's 5 s close timer; then the idle cameracaptured (about 205 MB with sweetcam and Chlorophyll in-process) went over its jetsam `InactiveHardMemoryLimit` of **50 MB** (com.apple.jetsamproperties.N104.plist, Daemon/Override/com.apple.cameracaptured; ActiveSoft 1900) and was killed, and the flashlight relaunched it: every 7-10 s from boot whenever no app used the camera. **Two fixes:** (1) sweetcam starts the sensor at Start only (`/private/var/tmp/sweetcam.eager` = the old way); observed alone: no more sensor starts, the kill cycle went on. (2) cameracaptured's InactiveHard limit 50 -> **384 MB**: live on the phone (`/System/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.apple.jetsamproperties.N104.plist`, original in `/var/root/jetsamproperties.N104.before-cam.plist`; sweetcam before the change in `/var/root/sweetcam.before-lazy.dylib`) and in the root build (`root_tweaks18.camera()` -> `inactive_jetsam(CAMERA_JETSAM)`, the helper shared with Chlorophyll's iconservicesagent limit; root image NOT rebuilt). **Observed after a reboot on 130f (18:49):** one `exec cameracaptured`, no kill and no sensor start in 3.5 min (RSS 165 MB); Camera opened from it: preview (the stream starts at Start), a 12 MP photo (IMG_0023, `4 frames (+1 after the last)`, no fault), Home: the stream stopped (853 frames), cameracaptured stayed up idle (5.5 min, RSS 155 MB). Not tried by hand since: the flashlight button (it goes through sweettorch's own device and `kern.sweet_torch`, not sweetcam's streams, so it should not have changed).
* **CAMERA ON THE HOME SCREEN AND THE LOCK SCREEN (2026-11-09 19:00-19:15, user: "can you look for and fix why there is no camera app on the launcher, also camera shortcut from lockscreen is still greyed out").** **Cause (observed):** Camera.app's Info.plist has `SBAppTags = [still-camera]`, and MobileGestalt answered `still-camera`, `rear-facing-camera`, `RearCameraCapability` and `auto-focus-camera` false (`camera-flash` true from /product/camera "flash"): SpringBoard hid the app and dimmed the lock screen's button. MobileGestalt reads `IODeviceTree:/arm-io/isp` "camera-rear" and "camera-front" (and many /product/camera properties); it keeps device-tree property names hashed like its keys, base64(md5("MGCopyAnswer" + name)): hashing every property name of n104ap.adt decoded 166 of the ~1680 hashes in its strings, among them `X9NA3D+PguwY0i0Uffl07Q` = /arm-io/isp camera-rear. Our ADT had no /arm-io/isp. **Fix:** an /arm-io/isp node with only `camera-rear` = 1 (no compatible, nothing matches it; the kernel has no Apple ISP driver; no front camera): `tools/adt-haptics.py --rear-camera` -> `enxerto/out/dipper-n104-2x-wlan-gpu-hap-cam.adt` (otherwise identical to -hap.adt; the new default of `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh`), and `tools/mkadt.py` adds it for --board dipper (`rear_camera`). **Image 131** `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-131-camtag.img` (130f's kernel 3085f + that ADT, sha256 1c4db926824af233...). MobileGestalt's cache deleted before the boot (backup `/var/root/MobileGestalt.before-camtag.plist`); `tools/camera/mgq.c` (MGCopyAnswer KEY..., on the phone /var/root/mgq) then gave still-camera, rear-facing-camera, RearCameraCapability, camera-flash, video-camera true, front-facing-camera and auto-focus-camera false. SpringBoard put Camera at the end of home page 2; page 1 was iOS's default page minus Camera, so IconState.plist got it back after Photos (backup `/var/root/IconState.before-camtag.plist`) and the phone was rebooted on 131. **Observed (19:11-19:13):** Camera on page 1 after Photos; tapping it opens Camera with the live picture; the lock screen's camera button is no longer dimmed (as bright as the flashlight's); a left swipe on the locked lock screen opens Camera with the live picture; a photo from there (IMG_0024, `4 frames (+0 after the last)` = the sink-B path of 3085f, guards unchanged 5 frames later). Not tried by hand: pressing and holding the lock screen's camera button (sweettouch has no long press).
* **FULL-SCREEN DISPLAY: THE PANEL'S OWN SHAPE (2026-11-09 19:15-19:40, user: "can you fix the display resolution? there are two small black vertical bands on the edges ... dipper should be 1080 x 2248").** **Cause:** iOS drew the iPhone 11's canvas, 414x896 points at @2x = 828x1792 (aspect 2.164), and the kernel's display scaler (QSEED3, `sweetfb_hw=1`) fitted it onto the 1080x2248 panel (aspect 2.081) with `sweetfb_scale=1` (fit, bars): 2248/1792 = 1.2545 on both axes = 1039 px wide, ~20 px black at each side; real touches at the sides were mapped through the same fit, so they were slightly compressed too. **Fix:** a canvas of the panel's own shape, **414x862 points at @2x = 828x1724** (1.3043 on both axes = 1080x2248.7), and `sweetfb_scale=2` (stretch: x 1080/828, y 2248/1724, the two differ by 0.03 %). `tools/adt-canvas.py` sets /arm-io/disp0 canvas-width/height of an ADT already built (`enxerto/out/dipper-n104-2x-wlan-gpu-hap-cam-862.adt` from -hap-cam.adt); `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh` now defaults to that ADT and to `sweetfb_scale=${SWEETFB_SCALE:-2}`; README's mkadt line uses --points 414x862. Real touches go through SweetHID's inverse of the same transform (fScale/fPad/fScale*Num/Den), so they follow by construction (not checked with a finger by me; sweettouch injects normalised positions and bypasses it). **Observed (test image 132t, 19:24, and 132, 19:30):** `SWEET FB: hw scaler programmed: src 828x1724 dst 1080x2248 at 0,0`; MobileGestalt main-screen-width/height 828/1724 (cache deleted before, backup `/var/root/MobileGestalt.before-862.plist`), still-camera true; screenshots (research/shots/res862/, not in git) of the lock screen, home screen, Settings and Photos laid out right (status bar, dock, home indicator, no red banner); a sweettouch tap on Settings' icon opened Settings. The bands themselves can only be seen on the glass: not seen by me. **Camera regression found on the way (my sweetcam change of 18:44):** with the sensor started only when an app starts the camera, the first stream of a boot came minutes after boot and the three 2.8 MB preview buffers could no longer be allocated contiguously (132t: `no contiguous memory for buffer 1/2`, black viewfinder; before, the flashlight cycle had allocated them seconds after boot). **xnu 3086b** (in 3086, tree a2e15e3): the preview buffers from any wired pages (`kmem_alloc`; the write master reaches them through `sweet_smmu_map32_pages` since 3086). **Image 132** `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-132-862.img` (kernel 3086b sha256 66544b96972e4423..., ADT -hap-cam-862, sweetfb_scale=2; image sha256 3f929ee6d004fdb4...; `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh KERNEL OUT` with its new defaults makes the same bytes), RAM-booted 19:30: Camera opened at 10 min uptime: the buffers mapped page by page, preview running, a 12 MP photo (IMG_0025, `4 frames (+1 after the last)`, no fault). The first `stream: did not start` of each boot is sweetcam's first try before it loads the sensor sequence (seen on earlier boots too). **User on image 132 (19:40): "display edges look good but icons on the top are almost inside the notch, earlier they were better".** Measured on the screenshots: with 414x862 iOS lays the status bar out differently (clock 57 -> 70 pt, Wi-Fi 348 -> 315 pt, battery 381 -> 344 pt from the left), i.e. not the iPhone 11's layout; UIKit has providers per known screen (`_UIStatusBarVisualProvider_Split828` = XR/11, Split1125, Split1170, ..., Fallback, CustomSplit) and 414x862 is none of them (which one it took and how it chooses: not found; MobileGestalt's main-screen-height follows the framebuffer, so it cannot be told 1792 separately). **Image 133** `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-133-896s.img` (kernel 3086b, ADT -hap-cam = the iPhone 11's 414x896, `sweetfb_scale=2`; sha256 33226bc41f59b5bb...; the new defaults of `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh`): `hw scaler programmed: src 828x1792 dst 1080x2248 at 0,0`, the whole panel at 1.304 across and 1.254 down (**4 % wider than tall**); MobileGestalt main-screen-height 1792 again (cache deleted, backup `/var/root/MobileGestalt.before-896s.plist`); the status bar is the iPhone 11's again (screenshot research/shots/res896s/): on the panel the clock is centred at ~148 px, Wi-Fi ~908, battery ~994 px from the left (132: Wi-Fi ~822, battery ~897). `tools/adt-canvas.py` stays for the 414x862 canvas (not the default).
* **OLED (AMOLED) BURN-IN: WHAT PROTECTS THE PANEL (2026-11-09 19:55, user: "something i wanna know now is that if OLED protection is there"; read-only look).** **There:** iOS auto-lock (on this phone `maxInactivity` 60 s, EffectiveUserSettings.plist) first dims the EA8074 (`SWEET DSI: brightness 2`, DCS 0x51), then asks the framebuffer for display off; on the Mi 8 there is no WLED, so SweetFramebuffer's vsync timer takes the `blackout()` path: `SWEET FB: display off: screen black in one step` (seen at every lock in today's log) = an all-black frame scanned out, AMOLED pixels dark (the panel and the MDP stay powered). The 2026-11-09 note "keeps showing the last frame at backlight 20" was read from screenshots (they show the canvas, not the glass) and the dim stage; not a lit frame after the off. **Not there:** no OLED-aware behaviour from iOS (the phone is an iPhone 11 to it, an LCD model); no pixel shift or static-content handling in the kernel; Bergamota fastboot (Enxerto) never dims or blanks (ui_tick only refreshes the charger text every 250 ms), so a phone left in fastboot shows the same lit screen indefinitely; a hard hang keeps its last frame lit until the power button (the 12 MP freezes today: the Camera screen lit for about 80 minutes, 16:16-17:40). The panel's own compensation, if any: not known.
* **PIXEL ORBIT AGAINST AMOLED BURN-IN (2026-11-09 20:00-20:25, user: "Yes, add it", after choosing our own measure over an OLED iPhone identity: iOS 26's dyld cache has no burn-in, pixel-shift, image-retention or OLED strings at all, so an OLED identity would bring a new screen geometry and @3x cost, not protection).** **xnu 3087** (`xnu/patches-12377/3087-dipper-display-pixel-orbit.patch`, research tree df2339a), SweetFramebuffer.cpp: with the hardware scaler the picture is 2N px smaller per axis (`sweetfb_orbit=N`, default 2 on dipper, 0 elsewhere, at most 8: 1080x2248 -> 1076x2244, 0.4 %), and its origin walks a serpentine over the (2N+1)^2 offsets of that margin, there and back, 1 px per step, one step every `sweetfb_orbit_s` seconds (default 120) of display-on time only (the clock stops while iOS has the display off); it starts on the centre cell (offset N,N). The move is made in `scanAddr()` with the next frame's CTL flush (`hwProgram()` rewrites OUT_XY/OUT_SIZE/QSEED3 steps), so it lands on a frame boundary; the margins are the mixer's border colour, set black (border fix). `sweet_fb_hw_dst[4]` publishes the rectangle actually on the panel; SweetHID maps touches through it, so they follow every step. The first 50 steps are logged (`SWEET FB: pixel orbit step K: picture at X,Y`). The boot-args field is full (606 of 607 bytes), so the orbit is on by kernel default rather than by a boot-arg; turning it off (`sweetfb_orbit=0`) needs a byte freed first. Covers sharp edges of static UI (status bar, dock, home indicator); a large bright area left for hours is auto-lock's job; a hard hang still keeps its last frame lit (a hardware watchdog would be needed). **Observed:** test image 134 (first build, 20:06): `hw scaler programmed: src 828x1792 dst 1076x2244 at 2,2`, then with the display kept on `pixel orbit step 1: picture at 1,0` and `step 2: picture at 2,0` two minutes apart: it stepped, but from the centre 2,2 to 1,0 (a 2 px jump: the walk started at index 0); fixed to start on the centre cell (index N*(2N+1)+N), rebuilt: **image 134** `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-134-orbit.img` (kernel 3087 sha256 26d587ccc6924cd4..., image 26a712811330dc67...; `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh` defaults), RAM-booted 20:12: starts at 2,2, no fault; first try of its check: the keep-awake loop (`sweettouch home` every 20 s) ran on the lock screen, where each press switched the display off or on, so too little display-on time; the user saw the display off ("display is off") and said to do it from the home screen. **From the home screen (20:24-20:30): the display stayed on through 16 presses (`kern.sweet_fb_display_off=0` each time) and the log has `pixel orbit step 13: picture at 3,2` and `step 14: picture at 4,2`**: 1 px moves from the centre, two minutes apart. Not checked: touches with a finger after a step (the mapping follows `sweet_fb_hw_dst` by construction).
* **CPU AT IDLE, WHERE IT GOES (2026-11-09 20:35-20:50, user: "can you check general performance, like cpu usage? is there something eating cpu without actual need?"; image 134, ~20 min after boot, USB and the kernel log listener connected; `/var/root/sweetcpu`).** **Display off, 60 s:** 21.0 CPU-s = ~4.4 % of the 8 cores: kernel_task 8.9 s (its `sweet` service threads, 30 s with `--kernel`: ufs sync 3.8 % of a core, usb net 2.4, ssc 1.5, bt 1.5, wlan 1.5, charger 1.0, gpu pm 0.7, keys 0.5), **ReportCrash 3.8 s**, backboardd 1.7 s, launchd 0.75 s, the rest small (mobileassetd and Spotlight indexing were busy in the first sample: post-boot work). **Crash loops since this boot (kernel CRASH lines):** PassKitSpotlightIndexExtension 12 x SIGABRT and com.apple.mobilenotes.SpotlightIndexExtension 6 x SIGABRT (both an ObjC exception thrown inside PlugInKit right at start: the extension never runs), MessagesBlastDoorService 10 x SIGTRAP (a Swift assertion in BlastDoor from its main), AegirPoster 2; jetsam: pkd, appstored, languageassetd. They are relaunched, so ReportCrash (~6 % of a core) and launchd work for nothing. **Accelerometer:** iOS asks 59 Hz while the display is on and 10 Hz after (`sensors: accel at 10 Hz (interval 100000 us asked)` at 603.9 s), but the SLPI kept delivering ~50 Hz (2972 samples between the status lines 60 s apart, display off): five times the samples iOS wants go through the ssc thread, SweetHID and backboardd. **UFS syncer (patch 0221):** a synchronous VFS sync + SYNCHRONIZE CACHE of the writable mounts every 5 s with polled I/O = its 3.8 %; needed (the HFS root has no journal and no syncer of its own), only its period could change. **Gyro calibration writes** by the SLPI (sns_gyro_cal_persist_s0.*, served by FastRPC to the iOS root's copy of the registry, not the persist partition): bursts, a few per minute at most. **Display on, home screen, untouched:** 7.3 CPU-s in 20 s = 36 % of a core (kernel 3.6 s, backboardd 1.8, SpringBoard 0.6, CollectionsPoster 0.1); the framebuffer gets ~10 full-screen swaps a second (100-111 per 10 s, `kern.sweet_fb_swaplog`: one 828x1792 layer alternating two surfaces, ~1.9 ms kernel copy each). In Settings, untouched: **0 swaps in 10 s**, so Core Animation does go idle and the home screen's ~10 fps is the bubbles wallpaper (CollectionsPoster) animating. Not changed yet: proposals are fixing or switching off the three crash loops, holding the accelerometer to the interval iOS asks, a longer UFS sync period (durability trade-off), a static wallpaper (the user's choice).
* **CPU FIXES: THE CRASH LOOPS OFF, THE ACCELEROMETER HELD TO ITS RATE (2026-11-09 20:40-21:05, user: "Yes, fix both").** **Crash loops, causes:** MessagesBlastDoorService stops in BlastDoor/Sandbox.swift: "BlastDoor cannot run unsandboxed." (string in the dyld cache next to "BlastDoor failed to enter post launch sandbox state"; this kernel applies no sandbox profiles); the Spotlight index extensions die in PlugInKit under `EXExtensionMain` before their code runs (CoreFoundation's raise; the exception text was not caught live, but PlugInKit's startup strings include "plugin has invalid sandbox or container: error %d path %s": very likely the same cause, a guess). A real sandbox is a project of its own, so they are switched off the way the speech extensions were: `QUIET_EXT_OFF` in `tools/renegade/root_tweaks18.py` (SWEET_QUIET=1 builds) now also has `PassKitSpotlightIndexExtension.appex` (PassKit.framework), Notes' `com.apple.mobilenotes.SpotlightIndexExtension.appex`, `RemindersSpotlightIndexExtension.appex` and MessagesBlastDoorSupport's `MessagesBlastDoorService.xpc`: renamed `.quiet-off`, Wallet's also taken out of launchd.plist's AppExtensions. Done live on the phone (20:43; launchd.plist original in `/var/root/launchd.plist.before-quiet2`; to undo: rename back, copy that file back, reboot); root image not rebuilt. **Accelerometer:** **xnu 3088** (`xnu/patches-12377/3088-dipper-sensor-rate.patch`, tree 4b840ce): a running stream is stopped before its new rate (one request per stream), and SweetHIDSensor hands on accel/gyro/mag samples no faster than 3/4 of the ReportInterval iOS set. Observed: the restart works (`accel stopped for its new rate`, `off`, `at 10 Hz`, `on` at 61.8 s), but the SLPI still sends ~50 samples a second for the fresh 10 Hz request (2972-2978 per minute): that is its floor, so the HID filter is what holds iOS to 10 Hz (the ssc thread still takes the 50). **Image 135** `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-135-quiet.img` (= 134 + 3088; kernel sha256 8766d890b3bcbccf..., image 2bfb92569e90f345...), RAM-booted 20:45. **Observed after 14 min:** no PassKit/Notes/Reminders indexer or BlastDoor crash (the boot before: 12 + 6 + 10 in 25 min); left: AegirPoster 2, jetsam kills of pkd, languageassetd, appstored, AppPredictionIntelligence 1 each; callservicesd, imagent, IMDPersistenceAgent, searchd up on their first processes. Display off, 60 s: ReportCrash 3.8 s -> 0, backboardd 1.7 -> 1.0 s; the total about the same (22.5 s) because iOS's plugged-in maintenance had started (mobileassetd 2.8 s, PerfPowerServices 2.7, runningboardd 1.4, dasd 1.2, nsurlsessiond 0.6, MobileAsset downloads): its normal work on the charger, not a loop. Not checked: Messages and Phone by hand without BlastDoor (iMessage/SMS do not work on this port anyway).
* **TELE AND FRONT CAMERAS ANSWER (xnu 3089, TEST image 136, 2026-11-09 21:10-21:30, user: "please continue working on the other camera work, start with the support for telephoto, then selfie camera").** **Hardware (live DT `dtb/dipper/live.dtb`, decompiled):** cam-sensor@1 rear tele: CSIPHY 1, CCI master 1 (TLMM 19/20), MCLK3 on TLMM 16, reset TLMM 43, enables VANA TLMM 121 (from PMI8998 BOB), VIO TLMM 36 (+ camera_viodd_ldo, TLMM 75), VDIG TLMM 39 (+ camera_vdig_ldo, TLMM 99); cam-sensor@2 front: CSIPHY 2, CCI master 0 (TLMM 17/18, the main sensor's bus), MCLK2 on TLMM 15, reset TLMM 104, VANA TLMM 80 (BOB), VIO camera_viodd_ldo, VDIG camera_vdig_ldo + PM8998 GPIO 9; tiles from pinctrl-sdm845-v2.c (16/19/20/36 south, 39/43 east, 80/104/121 north). **Module files** (our vendor partition, `research/camera-dipper/module/`, gitignored: s5k3m3sn03, liteon_s5k3m3sn03, s5k3t1, s5k3t1_qtech, ov7251): sensorDriverData words 5-9 = slave, address/data types, ID register, ID; power settings {type, value, delay ms}: S5K3M3 slave 0x20, ID 0xb001 at 0x0002; S5K3T1 slave 0x5a, ID 0x3141 at 0x0000; both VANA, VIO, VDIG 1 ms each, reset 12 ms, MCLK 24 MHz 10 ms. S5K3M3 modes: 0 = 4032x3024 30 fps 4 lanes 1.2 Gb/s (+ a 128x736 embedded/PD stream on vc 1), 1 = 2104x1560 30 fps 4 lanes 0.792 Gb/s. **xnu 3089** (`xnu/patches-12377/3089-dipper-camera-probe-tele-front.patch`, tree 4abcfb7 amended): `kern.sweet_cam=11` (tele) / `=12` (front): reads PMI8998 BOB (refuses unless ready; never votes it), saves every pin (refuses if one is set to another function), XO + titan_top on, the module order, MCLK from XO (19.2 MHz, as the main sensor's C2: no PLL needed), chip ID read over its CCI master's pins (the bit-banged I2C now takes another pin pair), the bus scanned, everything down and put back; SPMI allow-list: reads of BOB (SID 3 0xa0) and PM8998 GPIO 9 (0xc8), writes of GPIO 9's MODE_CTL/DIG_OUT_SOURCE. **Observed (image 136, `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-136-probe.img`, sha256 14f0d28f8bbec7a4..., kernel `xnu/out-dipper-local-3085/kernel.development.sweet.3089` af10640a8082f6cf...):** BOB STATUS1 0x94 (ready); all pins plain GPIOs; first build MCLK3 from PLL2 "did not start" (CBCR 0x80000001: PLL2 runs only inside the stream setup), fixed to XO; then **tele: chip ID 0xb001 at 0x0002 MATCHES, 0x30d3 at 0x0000 (the S5K3M3's model ID); on CCI 1 only 0x10 ACKs** (its actuator and EEPROM did not answer: probably their own supply, not switched by the probe); **front: chip ID 0x3141 MATCHES; on CCI 0 0x2d (the sensor), 0x50 0x51 (EEPROM)**. Both powered down after. Next: the tele's frames (CSIPHY 1, its sequence from the module file, its exposure/gain registers and colour order), then iOS: an iPhone 11 has no telephoto, so the plan is sweetcam switching the back camera's source to the tele from 2x zoom.

* **ZOOMING NO LONGER FREEZES THE VIEWFINDER (2026-11-09 22:30-23:40, user: "yeah it's right / but tapping the expand button freezed the camera"; sweetcam only, image 138 unchanged, commit after a2c2478).** **Observed before the fix:** after any change of `ZoomFactor` (the front camera's expand button, the back camera's zoom button) sweetcam went on delivering frames (its timing lines) but the display stopped (`kern.sweet_fb` swaps_s 0), and cameracaptured logged for every frame `VTRotationCeleste signalled err=-12914 at :1983`, `VTPixelRotationSession ... :3870`, `BWPreviewStitcherNode.m:4738 (err=-12914)`. **Cause:** CMCapture's preview stage, BWPreviewStitcherNode (methods and ivars in `research/camera-ios/stitcher-methods.txt`, local; a swizzle of `renderSampleBuffer:forInput:` says its setup), makes the viewfinder picture with a VTPixelRotationSession: back 1734x1300 -> 828x1792 turned 90, front 1654x1240 -> 828x1792 turned 270 with a vertical flip. A whole picture VideoToolbox turns in software (works here, 25 ms for 1734x1300 -> 828x1792); a part of one (`VTPixelRotationSessionRotateSubImage` with a source rectangle, which is what the stage does as soon as it zooms) it gives to Apple's scaler, which this phone does not have (`IOServiceMatchingfailed for: AppleM2ScalerCSCDriver`, printed in the self-test's process): -12914, the frame is dropped. **What did not work:** (1) pointing CMCapture's pointer-table entries for the two functions (found through its stubs, one each) at replacements: no effect, the stage's calls do not go through them (direct branches inside the shared cache is the guess; not disassembled). (2) A probe that made a rotation session inside cameracaptured and asked its supported properties crashed it twice ("stack buffer overflow" under VTPixelRotationSessionCopySupportedPropertyDictionary); removed. **Fix (`tools/sweetnet/sweetcam.m`):** (a) `entry_hook`: the first 16 bytes of `VTPixelRotationSessionRotateSubImage` and `...RotateImage` in this process's copy of the shared cache are rewritten to `ldr x16, [pc, #8]; br x16; <address>`; the four instructions they replace (both begin pacibsp, sub sp, stp, stp: `d503237f d10603ff 6d0e3bef 6d0f33ed` and `d503237f d103c3ff 6d053bef 6d0633ed`; anything position-dependent there and the function is left alone) run from a landing in sweetcam followed by a jump to the function's fifth instruction, so Apple's function stays callable. Possible on Heartwood because of xnu patch 1004 (a process may write its private copy of shared cache pages) and `vm.cs_process_enforcement=0`; a page is not executable while it is written, so the landings have a 16 KiB section of their own (`__TEXT,__sweetland`). (b) `rot_either`: Apple's function first; when it fails, the same on the CPU: `turn_scale_420` (turn 0/90/180/270, flips, crop and scale in one bilinear fixed-point pass over 8-bit 4:2:0, 16 pieces through dispatch_apply; `m2m_scale` when nothing turns), turn and flips read from the session (`VTSessionCopyProperty`, works), else the stage's own. After three failures of Apple's the CPU goes first (no more error lines) and Apple's is only asked for what the CPU path does not do (other pixel formats). `/private/var/tmp/sweetcam.norot` leaves VideoToolbox alone. (c) Frame metadata now carries `ZoomFactor`, `TotalSensorCropRect`, `SensorRawValidBufferRect`, and each buffer `ValidBufferRect`; with them the stage takes the sub-image path from the first frame (source rectangle 40,30 1654x1240 of 1734x1300 -> output rectangle 0,268 828x1106, at 1x and at 2x alike), so the CPU turn is the viewfinder's normal path now: 5-10 ms a frame. Whether that 4.6 % inset makes the viewfinder's field differ from the photo's was not checked. **Self-test (`tools/camera/rottest.c` + exported `sweetcam_rot_selftest`, outputs to PNG with `tools/camera/yuv2png.py`; runs outside cameracaptured, no restart needed):** both entries rewritten; a test picture through the public function: whole picture Apple's own result (0), a crop `Apple's alone -12914; through the entry 0 in 9.6 ms`; the CPU's output against Apple's for a whole picture in all 16 combinations of turn and flips: mean difference 0.03 of 255 with the flips taken as of the output (76.7 for 90/270 with one flip when taken as of the source): the CPU path turns and mirrors as VideoToolbox does. **Observed after the fix (23:28-23:37, sweettouch + screenshots, `kern.sweet_fb` swaps_s; final build sha256 c041237122e548a8... running since 23:36):** back camera opens at its remembered 2x on the telephoto, live (15-20 swaps/s); tap on the zoom button at 2x -> 1x, live (30/s); a drag on the zoom button (`sweettouch swipe 187 590 60 590 900`; Camera logs `Zoom start: [Drag](BackWide-2.1)` ... `Zoom ended: [Drag](BackWide-5.0)`) 2.1 -> 5.0, 4.9 -> 3.4, 2.6 -> 1.0 (main sensor from 1.79), 1.0 -> 1.3: live after each; front camera: the expand button twice (zoom crop 0.77 <-> 1.00), live at 15/s both ways; photos IMG_0033 (back at 1.3x, 2016x1512 from the 12 MP frame's 3134x2350 centre) and IMG_0034 (front, from 1980x1484); no `err=-12914` line in 40 s of log, no cameracaptured crash report after 22:50. **Seen on the way, not fixed:** (1) A tap on the zoom button at 1x does not go to 2x: Camera logs `Will change to: Photo/BackSuperWide(...) from: Photo/BackWide(...)` (the iPhone 11's 0.5x camera, which sweetcam does not offer); once the stream was stopped and started again on the same sensor, otherwise nothing happened. The telephoto is reached by dragging on the button (or pinching, not testable with one finger), not by a tap. **Fixed 2026-11-10 00:10, and the reading of it corrected: bullet "A TAP ON 1x GOES TO 2x".** (2) One boot of image 138 (23:14) lost the regulator bus early: `SWEET RPMH: TCS0 done=0 irq=0 idle=0x1 control=0x1010000 cmd-status=0x10101/0x10101/0x10101`, `timeout; TCS quarantined` during a bus vote while the modem came up; every later vote of that boot was refused ("previous uncertain transaction"), the camera could not get L22 (`L22 vote failed (5)`, `stream: did not start`) and Camera's viewfinder stayed black. The next two boots were fine; it is the only such timeout in `research/camera-ios/klog-136.log` (this evening's boots). (3) launchd did not start cameracaptured again for more than 7 minutes after its third kill in about 20 minutes (Camera open and asking); a reboot was quicker. After a boot, one or two kills restart it at once. **Phone state:** the new sweetcam.dylib is in `/usr/local/lib` (not in the root image, as before); `/var/root/rottest`, `/var/root/sweetcam-test.dylib`, `/var/root/rot.out.*` are test files. **Not verified:** video, zoom by pinch, the rotation path for 10-bit or BGRA previews (they still go to Apple's only), the user's own look at the zoomed viewfinder.

At this start `kern.sweet_pon_reasons` read `on: pon1; last power-off: ps-hold`, 0x8c0 = 0x20. With the cable out the power off stays off. One boot, in order: black 185 mA, then the storage link asleep 105 mA. The readings drift down by tens of mA over minutes within a boot (not understood; the gauge at small currents, or the phone really settling), so only the big steps mean something: about 1.2 W before, 0.4-0.5 W now. **Added since the first commit (ba485c7):** `ufs_auto_hibernate` (AHIT 10 ms, as xnu 3054) at the start of the charging screen and of fastboot, off for the length of a flash; `oem load`, `oem tune:ufsh8:<ms>`. * **POWER OFF: BERGAMOTA NEVER SWITCHED THE PHONE OFF; A FIX IS WRITTEN, NOT YET ON THE PHONE (2026-11-13 12:20-13:00, user: "can you check the poweroff system of ios/bergamota / it was kinda fixed but phone even with bergamota power off mode felt hot and battery was going down quickly / after turning off from twrp, it really got off (after all night phone was charged and cold)").** The phone was not connected during this work (no fastboot device, no USB network): everything below is read from the code or built and host-tested, **nothing ran on the phone.** **What the user means by "bergamota power off mode" I did not ask:** my reading is either Enxerto's charging screen after it has gone dark, or the fastboot screen; both are covered. **Read in the code (observed):** (1) iOS's power off (xnu 3074, `sweet_reboot_poweroff`) is the same PMIC sequence as Linux's (PM8998 PS_HOLD type 4, PS_HOLD low); Linux, and so TWRP, configures PM8998 only (pm8998.dtsi `qcom,system-reset`; no `qcom,secondary-pon-reset` in the tree's dtsi), so there is no step TWRP does that iOS lacks. (2) Enxerto had no power off at all, only `reset`/`hw_reset`. (3) Its charging screen (`charge_run`) looped for ever: `delay_ms` spins on the counter, after 20 s idle the Mi 8 gets black pixels (no WLED on an AMOLED) with the panel, the MDP and the SoC still on, and nothing looked at whether the cable was still in: on battery it ran until empty. (4) Bergamota fastboot waited for ever too, its bright full-screen picture lit, the command wait polling the USB controller in a tight loop; no power-off command, no key. Every reset, panic and power-key start ends there (`boot` holds it). The one old figure: on a 1.5 A port the battery got +1.2 A in fastboot, so the phone took roughly 2 W there (my arithmetic from that bullet, not a measurement). **So the likely story (a guess until tried on the phone):** iOS is powered off; if a charger is in or put in later the PMIC starts the phone (every start seen so far had PON1 as its reason, cable in), ABL boots `boot` with `androidboot.mode=charger`, the charging screen goes dark after 20 s and looks off while a core spins; or the phone sat in fastboot. TWRP's night: a real PMIC power off with nothing starting the phone again. **Fix, commit ba485c7 (Enxerto only; no kernel change):** `enxerto/power.c`: `power_off()` (charger registers back to ABL's, `pmic_pshold_type(4)` = 0x85b enable off, 1 ms, 0x85a type, enable on, read back; PS_HOLD = 0; PSCI SYSTEM_OFF after 2 s; type put back if still on), and waits in WFE on the generic timer's event stream (`power_idle_init` checks it once: eight WFEs in 2..40 ms, else the old spin; `bergamota.idle=0` opts out). Charging screen: the cable out for 3 s powers the phone off. Fastboot, while waiting for a command: Power held 3 s (seen up first; not with Volume Down) and `fastboot oem poweroff` power off; five minutes without a USB host power off on battery, and on a charger only blacken the screen (USB stays up; a host or a key lights it, and the charger going then powers off). The fastboot screen's hint line says so. `pmic.c` now lets exactly PM8998 0x85a/0x85b through besides WLED and the seven charger registers. Design note `docs/BERGAMOTA_POWER.md` (with the list of what to try on the phone). **Built:** `BOARD=dipper IMGSUFFIX=-power enxerto/build.sh`, rc 0, fastboot_test 525 checks 0 failures (two new, `oem poweroff`), no absolute relocation; `enxerto/out/bergamota-fastboot-power.img` sha256 33c5397ebb848a39..., `enxerto/out/charge-test-power.img` 91dea4256e9f48e6.... **The images under the usual names are still the old ones** (`enxerto/out/bergamota-fastboot.img` cc6f35b6822bfa5a..., put back from `research/enxerto-before-power/` after the build overwrote them; note that file's `enxerto-boot.img` there is the last iOS boot image `dipper-mkboot.sh` left in `enxerto/out`, 22 MB). **Careful:** `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh` builds Enxerto into every iOS boot image, so images made from now on carry this untested code in the Enxerto that runs when ABL boots the image itself (a RAM boot through the flashed Bergamota does not run it). **NOT DONE, needs the phone and, for the last step, the user's word:** RAM-boot the test image from Xiaomi's fastboot (`sweetreboot fastboot` from iOS, or Power + Volume Down), then the list in `docs/BERGAMOTA_POWER.md`: does it start (a WFE that never came back would hang at once), `oem poweroff` with the cable in (does the phone stay off or come back into the charging screen?), the key, the five minutes, the unplug on the charging screen, battery current before and after, iOS's power off on battery and with the cable; flash to `boot` only after that. **Not looked at:** stopping the display's autorefresh while black, the CPU clock, whether the charging screen should simply switch the phone off once it has shown the level (TWRP's night says a phone that is off still charges).
* **THE MICROPHONE'S LINK RECOVERS BY ITSELF: xnu 3093, DEFAULT IMAGE NOW 141 (2026-11-10 17:35-18:20, user: `Do this task here: "Kernel: recover the mic after a codec port overflow"`).** **DEFAULT IMAGE: `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-141-mic.img`** (sha256 e6cece0fbac4c1f8..., kernel `xnu/out-dipper-local-3085/kernel.development.sweet.3093` sha256 96232dba09c6d716..., same ADT and boot-args as 140; `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh KERNEL OUT`). Patch `xnu/patches-12377/3093-dipper-mic-channel-recovery.patch` (commit 9da4bc9; research tree b6934db; bsd/dev/dipper_audio.c only; built with `tools/xnu-local-build.sh --remake 26.5`, rc 0). **The fault (bullet below, "THE MICROPHONE WAS SILENT ON THAT FIRST BOOT"):** one boot whose every capture read exact zeros, the codec's TX port 7 having reported an overflow (status 80 00, source 01) right after the channel was set up. **What it was not (observed):** in the log the six good boots before it brought the codec up 148-590 s after boot with no speaker playback before; the bad one at ~1298 s after one speaker playback. A boot of 140 with the speaker played first (`sweetplay` of 3 s of zeros, player on/off in the log, then `sweetrec 3`): microphone fine (-52 dBFS, status 00 00). The long wait before the first capture was not tried. The fault never came back: 1 boot in 12 so far. **3093, three parts:** (1) stage 6 is now a try (`cx_port_up_once`) inside a loop: a set-up that ends with the port's overflow bit, or whose manager messages fail once the AFE port runs, is taken down (`cx_port_down`: DISCONNECT_PORT, port configuration 0, interrupt clear, CHAN_CTRL remove, RECONFIG_NOW, AFE SLIMBUS_0_TX stop; all acknowledged on the phone) and set up again, three tries. (2) Samples decide: until a capture of the boot has delivered a sample that is not zero (`cx.tx_proven`; cleared by any take-down and by a second of exact zeros while capturing), `rec_start` reads the capture's first 300 ms, and on "only zeros" (or no samples in 800 ms) closes the capture, takes the channel down, sets it up and opens the capture again, twice at most. (3) Tests on the stage sysctl (`/var/root/sweetsys kern.sweet_codec=N`, then `sweetsys kern.sweet_codec` for the log): 16 = the next set-up pretends an overflow, 17 = take the channel down and set it up now (no capture running), 18 = DISCONNECT_PORT behind the driver's back. **Observed on the final image (two cold boots, 18:07 and 18:13: status 00 00, "the mic's channel delivers samples", -40 to -50 dBFS):** 16 then 17: "the codec's port reports an overflow (set-up 1 of 3): the channel is taken down and set up again", second set-up clean, capture fine. 18 then `sweetrec 2`: "only zeros in the first 300 ms: the mic's SLIMbus channel is taken down and set up again", "delivers samples after the redo", real levels from the first second (so a disconnected port reads as exact zeros, like the bad boot, and the redo cures that). 20 times 17 followed by `sweetrec 1`: 22 of 22 captures delivered samples at once. Through iOS: Camera movie IMG_0007.MOV, sound track AAC 105.6 kbit/s, rms -20.2 dBFS, 0.1 % of samples zero (the room was not quiet); the recording's start and stop tones played (kernel player on/off, all statuses 0). **Two things learned on the way (observed, test builds of the same day):** (a) a set-up that follows a take-down often reads source 04 or 06 (closed, underflow; 14 of 20) and works all the same, so only the overflow bit counts as a fault; (b) **Linux's order is worse here:** with the codec's port enabled right before CONNECT_SRC (where `wcd9xxx_cfg_slim_sch_tx` enables it) instead of first, 9 of 22 captures after a set-up began with 300 ms of zeros, none with the overflow bit, all recovered within two redos; the order of 3060 (port enabled, three register reads, AFE port configured and started, then the manager's messages) is kept. So a dead channel can show nothing in the port's status, and a connect that follows the enable too closely is one way to make one; whether the bad boot's was that is a guess (under load the gap gets longer, not shorter). 12 take-downs and set-ups with 16 `yes` loops running, old order: no overflow. **Not shown:** that 3093 cures the original fault (it did not come back to be cured); what a dead start costs the caller was not timed (by the code: 300 ms of reading, then the redo; guess, about a second); twice the first second after a redo held a full-scale click (peak 0.0 and -2.8 dBFS). Voice Memos, calls, the earpiece and Bluetooth were not exercised on 141. **Housekeeping:** the session restarted before this work, the scratchpad was emptied (the screenshot helper and the movie inspector are gone; `shot.sh` written again and kept in `research/helpers/shot.sh`) and the kernel console listener had stopped (restarted 17:40, same log `research/camera-ios/klog-136.log`, markers "=== boot 141 ..."). The Siri sheet still comes up at the first power button press after each boot, now with "Don't Use Siri"; left with the home button, no choice made. Phone: on 141 since 18:13, Camera closed in photo mode.
