* **MOVIES ARE 16:9 AND PLAY ON THE PHONE (2026-11-10 14:20-14:30, user: "yeah make 16:9, then, check phone playback"; sweetavc + sweetcam, commit 4ba8e49).** **Why they were 4:3 (observed with `/private/var/tmp/sweetcam.trace` and CMCapture's log):** iOS 26's Camera keeps one capture graph for photo and video. Video mode does not pick a 16:9 format (the back camera offers sixteen, 1920x1080 at 60 and 240, 3840x2160 at 30 and 60 ... as `/var/root/sweetcamtest` lists them); it stays on `VC 420f/4032x3024, 15/1-30/1`, stream FormatIndex 0 "Photo", PrimaryScaler `CropRect 4032x3024 at 96,72 -> 1504x1128`, and does a `liveReconfigureForOutputAspectRatio` (`PrimaryCaptureRectModification:1`): the preview stage then crops the frame's 16:9 middle (0,141 1504x846) for the viewfinder, and the movie gets the same 4:3 buffers (`"VideoScaler_StabilizationEnabled" = 0`: no stage of ours between them that would crop). **Fix:** the encoder records the part the viewfinder shows. sweetcam's rotation fallback (`rot_cpu`), which sees the preview stage's source rectangle every frame, calls `sweetavc_set_capture_rect(frame w, h, x, y, w, h)` when that rectangle's shape differs from the frame's by more than 5 % (else "whole frames"); sweetavc, when x264 opens at a recording's first frame, takes that part if the session's frames have that size (even offsets: 0,140), gives x264 the planes from its first pixel and makes the format description from the smaller size. **Observed:** `of 1504x1128 frames the viewfinder shows 1504x846 at 0,141`, `encoding 1504x846 at 0,140 of the 1504x1128 frames`; back camera IMG_0052.MOV: avc1 **1504x846**, 222 frames in 7.42 s = 29.9 a second (29.1 ms a frame in x264), AAC 100 kbit/s, all frames decode on the Mac, the picture is the viewfinder's; front camera IMG_0053.MOV: 1504x846, 117 frames in 6.38 s = 18.3 a second, sound. **Playback on the phone:** a tap on Camera's thumbnail opens the last movie in the system viewer, which plays it in a loop (`PhotosPlayer ... seeking in AVPlayer` every 6.7 s for the 6.38 s front clip; two screenshots 1.4 s apart show different frames; 18-19 display swaps a second, the clip's own rate): iOS's software H.264 decoder does it. Not checked: whether the sound is heard (the viewer starts muted), the 30 frames a second back-camera clip in the viewer (my swipe did not change the item). **Limits:** 1504x846 is what the preview-sized frames hold of 16:9 (from the sensor's 1440x810 middle, developed at half size); a sharper or wider movie needs frames made for the movie rather than the viewfinder's.
* **THE BACK CAMERA'S MOVIES HAVE SOUND: A RACE IN SweetSpeaker'S MICROPHONE READER (2026-11-10 14:10-14:20, user: "Yes, fix sound"; `SweetSpeaker.driver`, by hand on the phone).** **Observed (the driver's own log, subsystem com.sweet.SweetSpeaker, for the silent recording IMG_0047):** `mic stop IO` at 14:00:55.715, `mic start IO` 188 ms later (Camera sets a movie recording up by stopping and starting the input), `mic: kernel capture on` at 56.894, `mic: reader stopped: 222720 samples in 4.64 s` at 56.895, and at that session's end `mic stop IO: 1202 cycles, 1160 without the kernel capture (zeros)`; yet a reader had read all the while (`reader stopped: 1278720 samples in 26.64 s` when the next session began). **Cause (`mic_thread`):** the reader left as soon as it saw no IO: it cleared `gMicThreadRunning`, then stopped the kernel capture (about a second) and only then cleared `gMicLive`. A start inside that second found no reader and made a second one, which started the capture and set `gMicLive`; the first, coming out of its stop, cleared it. ReadInput then gave zeros for the whole session while the second reader read on. Whether a session got sound depended on that timing: the front camera's recording (IMG_0048) had sound because its start came after the first reader was gone. Not the sub-port guess of the bullet below. **Fix:** one reader at a time: it keeps the capture for a second after IO ends (`kMicLinger`; a restart inside it costs nothing and the ring stays current), stops the capture and clears `gMicLive` before it decides to leave, and decides that under `gStateMutex`: when IO has come back meanwhile it starts the capture again itself. Built with `tools/audio/SweetSpeaker/build.sh` (sha256 b588381d223876a0...), put into `/System/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL/` (the driver before: `/var/root/SweetSpeaker.driver.before-linger`, sha256 efbb686c6f8c19f9...), audiomxd killed and back in 2 s (`SweetSpeaker: initialized, devices Speaker, Actuator, Mic, Receiver`). **Observed after it:** back camera, IMG_0049.MOV: 7.55 s, 218 frames, AAC at 100 kbit/s, peak 30931 and RMS 3602 of 32768, every sample non-zero, no all-zero 100 ms block; the driver: `mic stop IO: 388 cycles, 19 without the kernel capture`, `mic start IO` 160 ms later and no new `capture on` (the capture was kept). Front camera, IMG_0050.MOV: 6.66 s, 125 frames, sound (peak 30487, RMS 2677). Two plain recordings with `/var/root/sweetrec` 0.3 s apart: `4 s: rms -42.8 dBFS, peak -8.5 dBFS`, the second 3 s with 98.7 % of its samples non-zero. **Not verified:** Voice Memos itself, a call's microphone (the same reader), the speaker, earpiece and haptics after the audiomxd restart (only the microphone was exercised), how close the sound is to the picture (still the measured re-timing of the bullet below).
* **VIDEO RECORDING WORKS: CAMERA SAVES H.264 MOVIES (2026-11-10 13:20-14:05; the user, asked where the encoder should come from: "x264 library"; sweetavc + sweetcam + sweetzoom, image 140 unchanged).** **x264:** `tools/x264-build.sh` clones https://code.videolan.org/videolan/x264.git (0480cb0, build 165, GPL 2+) into `research/x264/src` (gitignored) and builds `research/x264/out/lib/libx264.a` for arm64e (NEON assembly, 8-bit 4:2:0, no CLI; its `pthread_create` renamed to `sweetavc_pthread_create`). Nothing of x264 is in git. **The plug-in interface (found with a probe encoder whose table slots only said they were called):** a VideoToolbox encoder is a CMBaseObject of class `VTVideoEncoderGetClassID()` with vtable { reserved, CMBaseClass, encoder class }; the encoder class on iOS 26.6.2: version, 1 startSession(encoder, session, CMVideoDimensions), 2 encodeFrame(encoder, frame, pixel buffer, CMTime *pts, CMTime *duration, frame properties, info flags out), 3 completeFrames(encoder, CMTime *), 4 copySupportedPropertyDictionary(encoder, out) (asked before every property), 5-6 not seen called. `VTRegisterVideoEncoder(codec, create)` is `VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo(codec, NULL, create)` (info in the middle). A session runs its encoder in the calling process only in a media server process (cameracaptured is one) or with `VTCompressionSessionCreateWithOptions(..., refcon, options, &session)` and `kVTCompressionSessionOption_AllowClientProcessEncode` = true; otherwise in videocodecd (-12908 there). **`tools/sweetnet/sweetavc.m` -> `/usr/local/lib/sweetavc.dylib`** (x264 inside: GPL as a whole; built by `tools/sweetnet/build.sh` when libx264.a is there; sweetcam dlopens it in cameracaptured, `/private/var/tmp/sweetcam.noavc` / `sweetavc.off` leave it out): registers for avc1; supported-properties dictionary that answers every key (an NSDictionary subclass: CMCapture sets some forty, many private), the ones x264 can honour used (bit rate, frame rate, key frame interval, profile, entropy mode, colour tags); x264 `zerolatency`, sliced threads, NV12 straight from the pixel buffer, 4-byte NAL lengths; one frame in, one sample buffer out through `VTEncoderSessionEmitEncodedFrame` in the same call. `b_vfr_input` must be 0 (1 holds every frame back by one: the first try gave "0 bytes for frame 0"). x264's threads start user-interactive (default-priority threads). Preset `ultrafast` (see below; `/private/var/tmp/sweetavc.preset` names another). **Timing in the test tool is meaningless:** `tools/camera/vtenc.m` (now also encodes test pictures; `VTENC_LIB=...sweetavc.dylib` loads our encoder in-process) gave 43 ms a 720p frame and 105 ms a 1080p one whatever the preset's threads: a process started over SSH has thread priority 4 (the background band; setpriority did not lift it) and Heartwood runs it on the small cores at 0.9 GHz (cpu0-3 50-70 % busy, cpu4-7 idle). **Two more things stood between the encoder and a movie:** (1) Camera recorded HEVC: `Failed to find desired codec avc1, using default of hvc1`: `+[AVCaptureMovieFileOutput availableVideoCodecTypesForSourceDevice:sourceFormat:outputDimensions:fileType:videoCodecTypesAllowList:]` leaves H.264 out when the camera supports HEVC and size x frame rate is over a limit; video mode runs on stream format 0 "Photo" here. `sweetzoom.dylib` (in Camera) now makes that list avc1 first and no hvc1 (`movie codecs for 1440x1080: Apple's list hvc1 avc1, ours avc1`). (2) A recording never ended: after the stop CMCapture's BWFileCoordinatorNode logged `flushing all buffers from recording staging queues` and nothing more, the file stayed without its moov atom and kept growing (silent AAC), Camera's button was back but nothing was saved. A probe of the node's fields (`/private/var/tmp/sweetcam.fcn`) showed it waiting for the audio to reach the last video frame's time: video at 4117 s, audio at 3092 s, both advancing in real time, both on the audio session clock (host time then 5183 s). **Fix (sweetcam, `fcn_render`):** audio buffers entering the coordinator are re-timed by the difference between the two, measured from the first buffers of each kind against the host clock (`the audio's time is -1055.321 s from the video's ... re-timed`), measured again only if it moves by 2 s; `/private/var/tmp/sweetcam.noavtime` off. Where the offset comes from (the microphone is SweetSpeaker.driver behind audiomxd's virtual input device) was not looked into; the sound and the pictures are then only as close as their two delays to that node (tens of ms, not measured). **Observed:** `sweetavc: H.264 encoder (x264 build 165) registered with VideoToolbox in cameracaptured: 0`; a recording: `an encoder made in cameracaptured`, `session started: 1504x1128`, `x264 open ... 6786 kbit/s, 30.00 fps, a key frame every 30 frames, high CABAC`; coordinator after the stop: state 1 -> 0 within a second; Camera: `didFinishRecordingToOutputFileAtURL`, `PersistenceController: added video to library`. **IMG_0044.MOV** (the first whole one): 6.52 s, video avc1 1504x1128, an AAC track, four metadata tracks; on the Mac AVAssetReader decodes all 154 frames, Quick Look shows the office, upright (the track's transform turns it). With preset superfast the encoder took 44-48 ms a frame and the movie had 23.6 frames a second: while recording all eight cores are 85-90 % busy (cameracaptured 57.5 CPU-s in 10 s; both clusters at their top frequency). With **ultrafast** 33 ms a frame: IMG_0046 281 frames in 9.5 s, **IMG_0047.MOV 223 frames in 7.52 s = 29.6 a second** (spacing mean 33.7 ms, longest 68 ms), 7.0 Mbit/s. **Front camera: IMG_0048.MOV**, 6.58 s, 119 frames = 18.1 a second, upright. **Sound:** the back camera's movies have a silent track: every sample 0 (AAC at 1 kbit/s), although the kernel says `SWEET AUDIO: capture running` and tccd grants cameracaptured and Camera the microphone. The front camera's movie has sound (peak 29494, RMS 2063 of 32768). My guess then (another microphone sub-port) was wrong: **fixed at 14:15, bullet "THE BACK CAMERA'S MOVIES HAVE SOUND"**. **Also seen:** the movie is 4:3 1504x1128 though Camera shows "HD" and a 16:9 viewfinder (it crops 1504x846 of the same picture): the N104 has 13 stream formats (Photo, Video-60, Video-120, Video-Binned-240 ...) and CMCapture runs video mode on index 0 "Photo"; real 16:9 1080p needs the right format chosen and a 16:9 picture from sweetcam. IMG_0043.MOV is the first, stuck recording, finished when cameracaptured was restarted: 4.4 s of video with 118 s of silent audio. IMG_0040/0041 are stray photos of mine. `ExcUserFault_SpringBoard-2026-11-10-135203.ips` appeared during the cameracaptured restarts (not read). cameracaptured was killed about eight times this hour and came back at once each time. **Phone state (by hand):** `/usr/local/lib/sweetavc.dylib` sha256 0ad857985b925bf2..., sweetcam 0eb722ddacea125f..., sweetzoom 025962ae30914a19...; `/var/root/vtenc`, `vtprobe`, `vtdec`, `clk`, `sweetavc-test.dylib` are test files. `root_tweaks18.camera()` installs sweetavc.dylib when it is built (not run in an image build). **Not verified:** playing a movie on the phone itself (Photos), the telephoto (2x) while recording, recordings longer than half a minute (heat: every core busy), how close sound and picture are, Live Photo movies (Live Photo is on: pref 2), slow motion, time-lapse, the pause and photo buttons while recording. **Out of reach this way:** 4K, 60 fps and the slow-motion modes of the GSMArena list: the frames are developed on the CPU from a 1920x1080 raw stream; that needs the phone's image processor and its Venus encoder (no drivers here).
* **VIDEO RECORDING: WHERE IT STANDS (2026-11-10 12:36-12:45, user, with GSMArena's Mi 8 list (main 4K 30/60, 1080p 30/120/240, 720p 960; selfie 1080p 30): "can you make videos supported"; a look only, nothing changed but the tools).** **Works already:** Camera's VIDEO mode: `Did change to: Video/BackWide(Auto_AutoFPS,Stereo_MixWithOthers,...)`, a 16:9 viewfinder with the "HD 30" badge, 30 swaps/s (sweetcam still on its Photo format 0, PrimaryScaler 1734x1300). **Missing: a video encoder.** `tools/camera/vtenc.m` on the phone: VTCopyVideoEncoderList has h263, jpeg, sjpg only. `VTCompressionSessionCreate` for avc1 and hvc1 succeeds with `com.apple.videotoolbox.videoencoder.h264.rtvc` / `.hevc.rtvc`, but every frame fails: the output callback gets -12908 (kVTCouldNotFindVideoEncoderErr), CompleteFrames -12782; 0 of 60 frames out at 720p and 1080p. So those are fronts for Apple's encoder chip. In cameracaptured, when a Live Photo's movie is asked: `AVE WARN: Register HEVC video encoder of AVE -1005`, `Register AVC video encoder of AVE -1005`, `VTVideoEncoderSelection signalled err=-12908`, then `PT (0x0): Encoder got ... property` lines with what CMCapture wants of the encoder: H264_High_AutoLevel, CABAC, 7998840 bit/s, 30 fps, ITU_R_709_2 primaries and transfer, ITU_R_601_4 matrix. **There for an encoder of our own:** VideoToolbox exports `VTRegisterVideoEncoder`, `VTRegisterVideoEncoderWithInfo`, `VTVideoEncoderGetClassID`, `VTVideoEncoderGetCMBaseObject`, `VTEncoderSessionEmitEncodedFrame`, `VTEncoderSessionCreateVideoFormatDescription`, `VTEncoderSessionSetPixelBufferAttributes`, `VTSelectAndCreateVideoEncoderInstance` (the plug-in interface; its class table has to be read from an encoder that exists, e.g. the h263 one). **Playback side:** a VTDecompressionSession for a 640x480 baseline H.264 stream's parameter sets is made (`VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported` 0 for H.264 and HEVC, so a software decoder; no frame decoded yet). **Not looked at yet:** what CMCapture asks of the stream when a movie really records (I did not get a recording started: my two taps on the record button landed in PHOTO mode and took IMG_0040/0041), the microphone in cameracaptured, the movie file and its way into Photos. **Limits whatever the encoder:** frames are developed on the CPU from the kernel's 1920x1080 raw stream (the preview picture is half that, 960x540), so 1080p at 30 fps is the ceiling without the phone's own image and video hardware (Spectra ISP, Venus encoder: neither has a driver here); 4K, 60 fps and the slow-motion modes are out of reach that way. **Seen:** `CAMUserPreferenceDesiredIrisMode` is 2 (Live Photo on; it was 0, last written 12:34, not by me as far as I can tell): each photo now also tries a Live Photo movie and logs the encoder errors above; the photos themselves are saved. * **THE TELEPHOTO AT 30 FPS, THE FRONT CAMERA AT 25, GAIN BEFORE LONG EXPOSURES (2026-11-10 12:25-12:35, user: "Yes, do it" to "Make the telephoto and front camera use shorter exposures and 30 fps in good light?"; xnu 3092, DEFAULT IMAGE 140).** **Before:** the stream held every sensor at `fll_max`, twice its mode's frame length: a steady 30 fps for the main (its mode is 60 fps), a fixed 15 fps for the telephoto and the front; and `c4_exp_split` took all the time `fll_max` allows before any gain: the telephoto 3815 lines = 56 ms at gain 1 in the lit office. **xnu 3092** (`xnu/patches-12377/3092-dipper-camera-frame-follows-exposure.patch`, research tree 2fd0854): `cam_prof.fll_min`, the stream's shortest frame (`C4_FLL_STREAM`, passed by the stream to `c4_up` and `c4_ae_step` in place of `C4_FLL_MAX`): main 2460 (unchanged), telephoto 2282 (its mode's own, 30 fps), front 2430. The front's mode has 2040 lines for a 1940-line picture, 1.6 ms of vertical blank, and the stream loop (a 2 ms poll) must write the next buffer's address inside the blank or the frame goes to the buffer just published; 2430 leaves 8 ms (25 fps); the telephoto's blank is 10.5 ms. `c4_exp_split` in four steps: the time alone up to `fll_min - 20` lines; then gain up to `C4_GAIN_KNEE` (4x); then the time again, the frame stretched with it, up to `fll_max`; then the rest of the gain (16x analog, the sensor's digital). With `fll_min = fll_max` (the main's stream) that is the old order. The one-shot `kern.sweet_cam=4` (frame length from the mode's own) now also takes gain up to 4x before stretching. No crash report. **Not verified (the office is lit):** the darker steps of the new order on the phone (gain 1-4x at full rate, then the frame stretching from 30 to 15 fps, then more gain), read from the code only; the front and telephoto handover under CPU load other than Camera's own; heat and battery at the higher rates (cameracaptured does more work: telephoto frames 4.1 MB, front 6.3 MB each, twice as many a second).
* **PINK LAMPS AND A PUMPING EXPOSURE FIXED (2026-11-10 12:06-12:25, user, in an office with ceiling lamps: "check also the 1x camera exposure, look at the lights in the office, they are pink / with the telephoto is only worse / try to fix please"; sweetcam + xnu 3091, DEFAULT IMAGE 139).** **Measured first (frames taken from Camera's running stream with the new `camframe -g N OUT`, which neither starts nor stops it; raw frames developed on the Mac by a scratch program doing sweetcam's preview arithmetic):** (1) the lamps are clipped in the raw frame (main: 2.7 % of the green cells at 1023, the telephoto 1.9 %), and the same frame developed with the white-balanced values clamped to full scale before the colour matrix has white lamps where the unclamped one has pink ones, on both sensors. (2) The exposure never settled: main sensor 1330, 933, 656, 461, 1233, 866, 608, 1320 ... lines (a new value every three frames, for ever), telephoto 3548, 2494, 3548 ... **Cause 1 (sweetcam):** a clipped pixel is R = G = B at the sensor's ceiling; the white balance (R x 1.9, B x 1.7 here) lifted red and blue above it and the colour matrix's negative terms took them off the green (green came out at 0.65 of full scale, red and blue clipped): pink. **Fix:** `isp_colour()`: white balance and scale per channel (`isp.k[3]`, in place of the folded matrix `isp.m`), clamp to 4095, then the matrix `isp_ccm` (its rows sum to 1, so a clipped pixel is white); used by the preview (`half_piece`) and both still paths (`full_demosaic`, `full_cells`). Also: the grey-world white balance now leaves out cells within 1/16 of clipping (`half_job.wsum`): the lamps pulled both gains towards 1 (that frame: R 1.59 with them, about 1.75 without), a green cast; the frame's mean (metadata, dark gain) still counts every cell. **Cause 2 (kernel, `c4_ae_step`):** a frame with 2 % or more of its metered greens clipped was never "on target" and was answered with 30 % less exposure whatever its mean (3078's highlight rule). With lamps in the picture the mean target and that rule fought: down in 30 % steps until the mean was far below the target, back up in one step, lamps clipped again. **xnu 3091** (`xnu/patches-12377/3091-dipper-camera-exposure-mean.patch`, research tree 5ccd749): the mean alone decides (target 150 of 959 above black, on target within 85-118 %); clipped pixels count in the mean as what they read. Built locally (`--remake`, rc 0): `xnu/out-dipper-local-3085/kernel.development.sweet.3091` sha256 3b706588826b7092..., image `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-139-ae.img` sha256 a8407f7db3f813d1... (ADT -hap-cam2 as 138). **Observed on 139 (booted 12:17, no RPMH timeout; the same office):** main sensor `exposure on target at frame 78: 1636 lines`, then 60 frames in a row at 1636 x 1.00 x 1.00; telephoto on target at its frame 6, 45 frames in a row at 3815 x 1.00 x 1.00; back on the main at frame 3 (each sensor keeps its own last exposure). Viewfinder screenshots at 1x and 2x: the lamps white, the ceiling white. Photos IMG_0037 (2x, telephoto) and IMG_0038 (1x, from the 12 MP frame, `1203 lines of 21231 ns x 1.00`): white lamps in both. The sweetcam part alone, on 138 at 12:15, already showed white lamps in the viewfinder. sweetcam.dylib sha256 9b028e6289b4b6d3... on the phone (by hand). **The telephoto "blown out" screenshot of the bullet below:** not looked into separately; its auto exposure does follow the light (3548/2494 lines in this office against 4544 x 16 x 2 on the dark table), so that picture was most likely taken while it came down from the dark setting, or on the upswing of the cycle. **Seen, left alone:** (1) the telephoto and the front camera run at a fixed frame length of twice their mode's (the stream passes `C4_FLL_MAX` as the frame length, as for the main sensor, whose mode is 60 fps): always 15 fps, and the exposure is taken as time first, gain last, so in this office the telephoto exposes 3815 lines = 56 ms at gain 1 (the main 1636 lines = 22 ms). Holding the time near 33 ms and using gain, or a frame length that follows the exposure (30 fps in good light), would be the next step for them. **Done the same day: bullet "THE TELEPHOTO AT 30 FPS".** (2) No anti-banding (exposure times are not multiples of the mains half-period); no banding was noticed in the screenshots. (3) The meter is a plain average: a bright window in the picture darkens the rest. **Not verified:** how fast the exposure follows a sudden change of light with 3091 (only the starts above), the front camera in this light, video. `/var/root/camopen.sh` on the phone now decides by a screenshot (an all-black one is a few kB: the display is off, power button first; `sweetopen` answering 3: locked, a swipe up).

C1-C4 and the sequence/frame sysctls answer EBUSY while streaming; the status sysctl does not block. One 8.8 MB contiguous allocation was refused on image 125 (nothing powered). **3080b (11c7d98):** three separate 2.85 MB buffers (frame + 256 KB guard each) and `sweet_smmu_map32(pa, len, &iova)` in place of 3076b's 1 GiB window: IOVA GiB 1 becomes a level-2 table, each range's 2 MiB blocks mapped in turn (0x40110000, 0x4045c000, 0x408ec000 this boot), earlier ranges reused. * **CAMERA AUTOFOCUS (xnu 3079, TEST image 124, 2026-11-08 17:30-17:40, user: "Autofocus first").** **The lens actuator** is inside the IMX363 module file (actuatorDriver at pool 0x1e4; there is no separate actuator file in /vendor/lib/camera): "dipper_imx363_ak7372_semco" = an **AKM AK7372**, 8-bit slave 0x18 (7-bit 0x0c), byte register addresses, a 10-bit code (dataBitWidth 10) written as a word << 6 (data shift 6) to 0x00/0x01, init 0x00 = 0x3c, 0x01 = 0x00, 0x02 = 0x00 (active), 100 us apart (the init code is 240), power VAF on then 10 ms. **VAF** = the live DT's actuator@0 cam_vaf-supply `actuator_rear_regulator`, a fixed 2.8 V regulator switched by TLMM GPIO 26 (SOUTH tile), fed by PMI8998 BOB. C2's scan saw 0x0e but not 0x0c: VAF was off then; with GPIO 26 high the bus answers at 0x0c 0x0e 0x1a 0x50 0x51 (0x0e still unknown; the module file also names an OIS "dipper_ois"). **3079 (`kern.sweet_cam=4`; `kern.sweet_cam_af` default 1, `kern.sweet_cam_lens` 0-1023 by hand; research tree 35a6d22, patch `xnu/patches-12377/3079-dipper-camera-autofocus.patch`, kernel `.3079` sha256 21ccfe8dfa66cfaf..., image `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-124-camaf.img` sha256 8f67ae612b7319c5...):** GPIO 26 joins the saved/restored camera pins; after the sensor's power-up VAF on, the module's init; once auto exposure is on target the exposure is held and contrast autofocus runs: coarse codes 0, 64 ... 960, 1023, then +-48 in steps of 16 around the best, each code scored on the frame finished 3 frames after the move (sum of squared differences of neighbouring greens' 8 high bits along even lines of the middle third), then the lens to the best code and the frame 3 frames later kept; the lens moves in steps of at most 96 codes 1 ms apart and goes back to 0 the same way before VAF is switched off. **Result (17:38, the user holding the phone toward a desk, "It's aimed now"):** exposure on target at frame 12 (2440 lines, 16x analog, 3.8x digital); coarse contrast 4.24 M at 0, 4.84 M at 192, 7.87 M at 320, 12.2 M at 384, 9.19 M at 448, 5.27 M at 512, falling to 3.35 M at 960-1023; fine pass peak 13.06 M at 400 (12.81 M at 416, 10.13 M at 432); kept frame at lens 400 is sharp (a laptop keyboard's keys legible; sent to the user, kept out of git; upside down in that hold: the sensor's mounting). 87 frames in the run, polled 30.21 fps vs the CSID's 30.04 (polling kept up this time). Everything put back afterwards, guard untouched. **Open:** EEPROM AF calibration (infinity/macro codes at 0x50, 8 KB per the DT's mem0) to narrow the sweep; the AK7372's ringing control and standby on power-down; continuous AF; PDAF (the sensor sends PDAF data on VC 1); streaming to userspace.
* **CAMERA AUTO EXPOSURE (xnu 3078-3078c, TEST images 123b-123d, 2026-11-08 17:05-17:22, user: "Exposure first").** **The IMX363's limits from its module file** (sensorDriverData exposure control, read with tools/camera/camx_v1.py's Module class): frame length 0x0340, line length 0x0342, integration 0x0202, analog gain 0x0204 (max 16.0; IMX code = 512 - 512 / gain, so code <= 480), one digital gain address 0x020e for all four colours (written to all four, 0x020e-0x0215, 8.8: 0x100 = 1x), vertical offset 20 (integration <= frame length - 20), black level 64 on all four channels, white 1023, pixel 1.4 um; the gain formula itself is in the sensor's .so, not the file. **3078 (`kern.sweet_cam=4`; new `kern.sweet_cam_frames` (default 60), `kern.sweet_cam_ae` (default 1), `kern.sweet_cam_lines`, `kern.sweet_cam_gain` (x100)):** two frame buffers (6.2 MB with the guard), the write master moved to the other one at each done; once the exposure has been the same for 3 frames (the sensor's latency) the finished frame is metered (green pixels of every 16th line pair, 8 high bits, black off; saturation = high byte >= 0xfc) against a target of 150 (10-bit above black, about 16 %); the next exposure goes in under group hold (0x0104) as integration lines (frame length stretched to at most 2460 lines = 30 fps), then analog gain to 16x, then digital to 4x, at most 8x up or 1/8 down a step, at least 30 % down when over 2 % saturates; the first frame within -15/+18 % of the target ends the run and is kept (`kern.sweet_cam_frame`); the next auto run starts where this one ended. 3078b: manual exposure keeps the lines as given. 3078c: the CSID's own start-of-frame timestamps (RDI 0 0x390 current, 0x398 previous, 19.2 MHz) give the frame period; polling with 20 us waits. Pictures right (walls, ceiling, a framed picture, a blue item), sideways (the sensor is mounted rotated) and soft (the autofocus actuator at 0x0e is not driven); sent to the user, kept out of git. **Frame rate (hardware timestamps):** 16.641 ms = 60.09 fps at mode 2's 1230 lines, 33.282 ms = 30.04 fps at 2460: the module's 60 fps is right. Counting write-master dones in software undercounts (47-55 fps over 30-60 frames, with 100 or 20 us waits, also right after boot): the polling thread misses dones; the 10 ms spacings of C4 were poll ticks. Missed dones do not spoil the kept frame (the sensor stops at the end of a frame, so the kept buffer always holds a whole frame) but can meter a buffer being rewritten. Guard untouched, no SMMU fault, everything put back after every run. **Open:** interrupts instead of polling (the VFE and CSID lines), continuous streaming to userspace (`/dev/sweet-camera`), autofocus (the actuator), lens shading / colour (a CPU ISP for iOS, C5), exposure in time units (line time 13.53 us in mode 2).

* **CAMERA: FORKS SURVEY, THE MI 8'S CAMERA HARDWARE AND A PLAN (2026-11-08 13:40-14:00, user: "start working on the camera, check the forks first, hakios made it work on a mtk fork"; read-only, nothing run on the phone but file reads).** **HakiOS, MediaTek (oosexgang/hakios-mt6768, MIT; commit 03383df, 2026-11-08; their claims, read through the GitHub API):** iOS 16.5's Camera.app shows a live preview from the Infinix Hot 20's main sensor (S5K JN1, 4080x3072, ~14 fps, run 575). Kernel `redwood_mtkcam.c` replays a sensor init captured from Android's I2C (kprobes on Android's imgsensor functions), writes and reads back the PMIC rails, and hands frames out as `/dev/redwood-camera` (the DMA writes 1 byte a pixel: pitch 4080, not 5100). iOS side `userland/camera/camera_device.c` (inside the capture daemon): a CoreMedia FigCaptureDevice with one FigCaptureStream, given to CMCapture's `BWFigCaptureDeviceVendor` in place of the one `H10ISP.mediacapture` makes, plus `camera_isp.c`, a CPU ISP (levels, AE, white balance, lens shading, colour matrix, tone curve, demosaic, scaling, NV12/BGRA). What the capture graph needed beyond the obvious (their doc `docs/camera-x6826b.md`): tccd running (camera permission); a processing session (FigCaptureISPProcessingSession, device slot 1); the stream's `ModuleInfo` with a sensorID that has an entry in the model's `CameraSetup.plist` (they used the iPhone X's 0x0343) and module IDs matching its FocalLengthCharacterization; `VideoOutputsColorInfo` answered; no frames before `VideoOutputsEnabled`/Start; frames made in each output's own BufferPool. Camera.app's icon needed SpringBoard's visible tags to include "still-camera" (MobileGestalt reads cameras from `/product/camera` and `/arm-io/isp` of the device tree). Not done there: saving a photo, video, autofocus, 10-bit, other cameras. Skeleton for other MediaTek phones: hakios-xnu-kernel 620c775. **HakiOS, Qualcomm (hakios-xnu-kernel `drivers/camera/hakios.camera.c`, POCO X5 Pro / SM7325, APSL as kernel code; their device table says "camera works, Camera.app (cam=5)"):** the closest hardware reference: CCI by hand, the sensors' power sequences and register tables read at run time from tables made of Android's CamX module files (`com.qti.sensormodule.*.bin`, their `tools/camsensor.py`, "Parameter Parser V3.0.1"), the CSID's test pattern through RDI 0 and IFE-lite 0 into memory first (cam=3), then the sensor through its CSIPHY (cam=4). Also yfl520/hackios-raphael (SM8150, Titan; docs/FORKS_SURVEY.md G5). **The Mi 8 (observed in `dtb/dipper/live.dtb`, decompiled):** CPAS hw version 0x170110 (Titan 170). CCI at 0xac4a000 (IRQ 0x1cc; masters 0 and 1 on TLMM 17/18 and 19/20). Four sensors: @0 rear main (CSIPHY 0, CCI master 0, MCLK0 GPIO 13 at 24 MHz, reset GPIO 119, VANA PM8998 L22 2.864 V, VDIG `camera_vdig_ldo` 1.35 V switched by GPIO 99, VIO `camera_viodd_ldo` switched by GPIO 75, GPIO 12 and 40 also listed); @1 rear tele (CSIPHY 1, master 1, MCLK3 GPIO 16, reset 43); @2 front (CSIPHY 2, master 0, MCLK2 GPIO 15, reset 104); @3 front IR (CSIPHY 1, master 1, MCLK1 GPIO 14, reset 25, VDIG `camera_ir_ldo` 1.5 V). Power domain `titan_top_gdsc` 0xad0b134. CSIPHY 0-3 at 0xac65000-0xac68000; CSID0 0xacb3000 / VFE0 0xacaf000, CSID1 0xacba000 / VFE1 0xacb6000, CSID-lite 0xacc8000. IFE SMMU streams 0x808, 0x810 (mask 8), 0xc08, 0xc10 (mask 8) on the apps SMMU (the one sweet_smmu.c already programs for the IPA). **Sensor tables from our own vendor partition (backup/dipper/vendor.img /lib/camera, extracted to the scratchpad with debugfs, never in git):** module files for imx363 (+liteon_), s5k3m3sn03 (+liteon_), s5k3t1 (+qtech), ov7251, imx333; tuning files semco/liteon_imx363, semco/liteon_s5k3m3, sunny/qtech_s5k3t1, sunny_ov7251. So: Sony IMX363 rear main, Samsung S5K3M3 tele, Samsung S5K3T1 front, OmniVision OV7251 front IR (which module maker this phone has is not read yet). Older CamX format ("ParameterParser V1.1.0"): header word 0x98 = entry table offset, count; entry 0 = symbol records of 64 bytes {id, name[32], kind, 4 words, offset into the pool}; entry 1 = the data pool. Read by hand so far (my own reader, scratchpad `mytools/camx_syms.py`): IMX363 slave 0x34 (8-bit), chip ID 0x0363 at register 0x0016, MCLK 24 MHz in its power setting. HakiOS's camsensor.py targets V3.0.1 and was not run here. **iOS 26.6.2 side (observed in the cache and on the phone):** CMCapture still has `-[BWFigCaptureDeviceVendor _createDevice:reason:clientPID:figCaptureDevice:]`, CMCaptureDevice has FigCaptureISPProcessingSession, CMCaptureCore has ModuleInfo / VideoOutputHandlers / PixelBufferHandler; H10ISP.mediacapture is still the ISP plug-in's name; capture runs in `cameracaptured` (where sweettorch.dylib already lives). `CMCapture.framework/N104/CameraSetup.plist` DefaultSensorIDs: Back 0x0503, BackSuperWide 0x0372, Front 0x0514, FrontInfrared 0x0d56 (copies in the scratchpad, not in git). **Plan (proposed, nothing started):** C1 a read-only kernel look (`kern.sweet_cam=1`): titan_top_gdsc and camcc state, the pins, CCI version registers. C2 the IMX363 powered as its module file says (L22 through RPMh, the GPIO-switched LDOs, MCLK0 24 MHz from camcc, reset), its chip ID read over CCI (expect 0x0363), powered down again. C3 CSID test pattern -> RDI -> IFE write master -> memory (SMMU streams mapped as for the IPA), checked as a picture on the Mac. C4 the IMX363's own frames through CSIPHY 0. C5 `/dev/sweet-camera` and a FigCaptureDevice in cameracaptured with a CPU ISP (HakiOS's approach, MIT: re-implement and credit), ModuleInfo sensorID 0x0503; the Camera.app icon via `/product/camera` in our ADT. Also needed: a proper reader for the V1.1.0 module files (tools/, output never in git).

* **iOS'S POWER OFF NOW POWERS THE PHONE OFF: xnu 3074, TEST image 120 (2026-11-07 20:50-21:36, user: "could you now fix the ios power off switch").** **Cause:** `SweetPlatformExpert::haltRestart` handled restart and panic types only; iOS's shutdown (launchd's reboot(RB_HALT) -> host_reboot HALT -> halt_all_cpus(FALSE) -> haltRestart(kPEHaltCPU)) fell to the stock spin, phone left on with a black screen (seen 2026-10-28). And dropping PS_HOLD alone only restarts: the firmware leaves the PM8998 PON's PS_HOLD reset type at 1 (warm reset; read at boot, see below). **3074** (research tree a2407de, `xnu/patches-12377/3074-dipper-poweroff.patch`, kernel `xnu/out-dipper-local-3040/kernel.development.sweet.3074` sha256 64f7bb60b6ed8cdb..., TEST image `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-120-poweroff.img` sha256 f71316f406b6f924..., default boot-args, = 119d + 3074; series check clean): kPEHaltCPU and kPEUPSDelayHaltCPU call `sweet_reboot_poweroff()` (bsd/dev/sweet_reboot.c): UFS cache flush, PON reason normal, PS_HOLD_RST_CTL 0x85a type 4 (SHUTDOWN) with PS_HOLD_RST_CTL2 0x85b bit 7 (enable) off around the change and 1 ms between (Linux pm8941-pwrkey.c pm8941_reboot_notify; downstream qpnp_pon_reset_config), then PS_HOLD 0; PSCI SYSTEM_OFF if still on after 2 s. A restart puts the boot type back if a power off changed it and did not happen. SPMI writes allowed to 0x85a/0x85b (sweet_spmi.c). `kern.sweet_pon_reasons`: the PON's latched reasons at this boot. PM8998's PON is gen2, so the reasons are at 0x8c0+ (downstream PON_OFFSET): PON_REASON1 0x8c0, WARM_RESET_REASON1 0x8c2, POFF_REASON1/2 0x8c5/0x8c6, then the PS_HOLD type found at boot. (The first build read gen1's 0x808, which showed 0x03 after a restart and after a power-key start alike.) **Tests (observed):** (1) 21:22 `reboot3(RB_HALT)` from a scratch tool (`/var/root/halt3`: launchd's userspace shutdown, then the kernel's halt): USB gone 2 s later, no device for 2+ minutes with the cable in; the user pressed power: "Yes, it started" (Bergamota fastboot). POFF_REASON1 then 0x02 (PS_HOLD), where before it was 0x80 (long power key: the user's force restart at 18:10). (2) A restart (`sweetreboot bergamota`) on 120: "on: pon1 (warm reset)", WARM_RESET_REASON1 0x02, PS_HOLD reset type at boot 1 (enabled): restarts still work and are warm resets. (3) 21:33 the user, iOS's slider (power + volume up): "Yes, it switched off"; after the power key: a cold start (0x8c2 = 0), last power-off PS_HOLD. PON_REASON1 shows bit 5 (PON1) after the restart and after the power-key start alike: what drives PON1 on the Mi 8 is not known (a guess: the power key reaches PM8998 through PMI8998). Not tried: Settings > General > Shut Down (same kernel path expected); a power off on battery alone. Charging while off: the user says the battery charges (Enxerto's own off-mode charging; bullet "DEFAULT IMAGE NOW 120"). **Phone now:** image 120, no SIM; image 120 the default since ~21:40 (user).

* **sweetcelld FIXED UP, AND THE HANG: THE IPA NOW ON AN SMMU BANK OF ITS OWN (xnu 3073c, TEST image 119c) (2026-11-07 18:10-18:56).** **Recovery:** the user force-restarted the phone (18:10); image 118 (no IPA) with sweetcelld installed ran 10+ minutes without the hang (Wi-Fi service past 240 s, SSH fine): sweetcelld's QMI traffic alone does not wedge it. **Likely cause (reasoned, not proven):** the IPA's streams were on the shared SMMU bank with USB (0x740) and the Wi-Fi copy engine (0x40/0x41), whose SCTLR has HUPCF 0: one outstanding context fault terminates every later transaction of the bank until the FSR is cleared, which matches USB receive and Wi-Fi dying together while non-SMMU threads (UFS, SLPI, charger) kept logging. **xnu 3073c** (`3073c-dipper-ipa-own-smmu-bank.patch`, research tree 4110fc1; kernel `.3073c` sha256 1a43ff60d5935726..., TEST image `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-119c-ipasmmu.img` sha256 af3c3afbde5a7beb..., default boot-args): `sweet_smmu_map_sid_ipa()` maps the IPA's streams to a second bank on the same identity tables with HUPCF 1; the IPA's receive thread reads that bank's FSR every second and logs/clears faults (`kern.sweet_ipa_status` "SMMU (the IPA's bank)"). On 119c: 0 faults in three boots so far, no hang (one boot watched 6 min with data up, another 8 min). **sweetcelld fixes:** (1) the Cellular Data switch: Settings reads it with CTServerConnection `kPacketGetProperty` naming `kEnableCellularData` (and `kCellularDataEnabled`/`kCellularDataCapable`/`kAirplaneMode`) and sets it with `kPacketSetPropertyWithReply` carrying `kEnableCellularData` as an INT64 (1/0), not a bool: now answered and taken (the user's taps on 118 had been read as 0). CoreTelephony's C API reads it as on (`cttest`: _CTServerConnectionGetCellularDataIsEnabled 1, GetCellularDataSettings 1 1 0, CTCellularDataPlanGetIsEnabled 1), **but the Settings pane still draws the switch OFF on first display** (its PSUICellularController keeps `cellularDataSettingInitialized`; CoreTelephony has kCTCellularDataSettingsChangeNotification and the notification keys kNotificationFlag/kNotificationEvent/kNotificationDict; the event number and the push format not found without a disassembler: open). iOS 26's Data Roaming calls (`getInternationalDataAccess:completion:`, `setInternationalDataAccess:status:completion:`) answered. (2) jetsam: a restarted sweetcelld was killed for its memory 10 s in (reason 7, per-process limit): the job now has CommCenter's label `com.apple.CommCenter` (com.apple.jetsamproperties.N104.plist: 36 MB active, 27 MB inactive, priority 190). (3) the modem crashed once at boot ("SFR Init: wdog or kernel error suspected", 1 s after WLFW appeared, during the Wi-Fi MSA hand-over) with sweetcelld already sending DMS ONLINE (one boot in four): the radio and the data path now wait until WLFW has been there 30 s (3 min without Wi-Fi); next boot: settled at 18:50:11, ONLINE, IPA 1-6, data session up 18:50:18, no crash. Relocatable, 3 PT_LOAD segments, extent 0x41c0. **Run on 119b (17:07-17:10, observed):** stage 1: BCM IP0 (unit 40, width 8) voted 0x3fff, SMMU sids 0x720/0x722 -> SMRs 9/10 in bank 3, IMEM block mapped; COMP_HW_VERSION 0x30050001 (IPA 3.5.1), ENABLED_PIPES 0x14, FLAVOR_0 0x90b0914, SHARED_MEM_SIZE 0x400 (8 KB at offset 0), GSI_STATUS 0, ROUTE 0 (nobody had touched the IPA). Stage 2: BCR 0x3b, QSB 0x48/0xc8, COUNTER_CFG 0xf0, ROUTE 0x1120052, LOCAL_PKT_PROC_CNTXT 0x7d0, local memory zeroed + canaries. Stage 3: PAS 15 INIT_IMAGE 0; **MEM_SETUP 0x8c400000 (ips_fw_region, the DT's qcom,ipa_fws memory-region) is refused with the exact extent 0x41c0 (status -3145798, image 119 at 17:03) and taken with it rounded up to 4 KB (0x5000)**; AUTH_AND_RESET 0; GSI_STATUS 1 (enabled). Stage 4: our channels 4/5/3/6 (command/LAN in/to the modem/from the modem, endpoints 5/9/2/10) started, the five immediate commands (IPv4/IPv6 route and filter table init, header init) completed (event code 2), no SMMU fault, QMAPv4. Stage 5: our service 0x31/1 announced at 1:0x4005; INIT_DRIVER (130 bytes, the 3.5.1 layout, TLV 0x18 skip_uc 0) to the modem's 0x31/2 at 0:0x1f; SMP2P "ipa" = 3; **the modem registered for indications (0x20), ACCEPTED INIT_DRIVER (result 0), sent DRIVER_INIT_COMPLETE (0x35)**; INIT_COMPLETE (0x22) sent; then its CONFIG (0x27, 63 bytes) and INSTALL_FILTER_RULE (0x23, 5229 bytes) left unanswered as Linux leaves them; its own SMP2P "ipa" entry appeared (0). Stage 6: rmnet0 (Ethernet-framed, ARP answered in the kernel by a made-up router MAC, QMAP mux 1) attached. DMS ONLINE: registered on LTE within 5 s. **Data call over `sweetqmi` (port 0x4004 keeps it):** DPM Open Port (0x2f/0x20, embedded endpoint type 4, interface 1, IPA endpoints 2/10): ok; WDA Set Data Format (raw IP, QMAPv4 both ways, 10 packets / 8 KB): ok; WDS Bind Mux Data Port (mux 1): ok; Set IP Family 4: ok; **Start Network Interface: ok, packet service connected, an IPv4 address on a /30 with gateway, two DNS servers, MTU 1500** (default profile 1; the addresses are not written here). Before the IPA (16:27) the same start had failed with 0x46 InvalidOperation. `kern.sweet_ipa_session` gave rmnet0 the address. **With host routes via rmnet0's gateway (`route -n add -host ...`): `sweetping -c 4 1.1.1.1` 4 of 4 answered, 46-51 ms (205 ms for the first, the radio waking); a DNS A query to the session's DNS server for example.com answered in 53 ms (2 records).** IPA counters: to the modem 12 packets (903 bytes), from it 5 packets in 7 buffers, no errors, no drops; LAN endpoint nothing. No modem crash, Wi-Fi up. New tool `tools/sweetnet/sweetping.c` (ICMP echo and a DNS query, `-I IFNAME`). **iOS apps over LTE (17:12-17:14, observed):** `tools/sweetnet/sweetnetcfg.c` now takes `-i IF -a ADDR -m MASK -r ROUTER -n DNS[,DNS] -s ID -p RANK` (defaults: ue0 as before); `/var/root/sweetnetcfg -w -i rmnet0 ... -s C1 -p First` published rmnet0 with the session's router and DNS and PrimaryRank First: IPMonitor made rmnet0 the unscoped default route (en0 and ue0 scoped); **`sweeturl https://example.com/` opened it in Safari and the page loaded over LTE** (screenshot `sweetshot`, not kept in git); rmnet0 then counted 747 packets out and 682 in within seconds (iOS's own background traffic moved to it too). Undone at 17:14: `sweetnetcfg -d -s C1` (killing the -w process does NOT remove the keys: SCDynamicStoreSetValue keys outlive their writer) and the two host routes deleted; en0 primary again, rmnet0 up with its address but no default route. **Not done yet:** the session is started by hand; the session is started by hand from the Mac (stages + datacall script in the session scratchpad); IPv6; throughput not measured; the receive thread polls every 2 ms while rmnet0 is up (battery not measured); after a reboot everything has to be done again.

* **GLASS PASS: MEMORYLESS ATTACHMENTS NO LONGER STORED OR CLEARED (gpu/metal a5b58cf, LIVE ON THE PHONE, NOT IN THE ROOT IMAGE) (2026-11-07 13:58-14:22, user: "Yes, try glass pass").** **What the glass pass is (new pass profile, which now names each colour attachment as format/IOSurface load/store and counts fetch draws):** `glass_background_no_bleed... attachment_clear... TimgA2S1Xhfu...`, 828x1792, 33-54 draws of which only 4-7 use framebuffer fetch, attachments `BGRA8Unorm(surf) L/S` (the framebuffer IOSurface, linear, loaded and stored) and `RGBA16Float d/S`. Every CoreAnimation pass has that second attachment, an RGBA16Float made MEMORYLESS (storage mode 3; `BGMTLTexture` did not keep the storage mode before), with DontCare load (cleared to zero by chl) and Store. **Turnip (read, mesa-turnip26):** any pipeline with input attachments in a dynamic-rendering pass sets `sysmem_single_prim_mode`, and `tu_autotune::get_optimal_mode` then returns GMEM, so every pass with a fetch draw runs in GMEM whatever chl does; the raster-order flag chl sets on fetching pipelines adds `SINGLE_PRIM_MODE FLUSH_PER_OVERLAP` in GMEM. **Tried (pass profile `12 0.0`, two `dipper-drag` rounds each, App Library and Today view screenshots):** `chl.noroa` (no raster-order flag, new experiment switch, off by default): glass pass median 5.5 -> 4.7 ms, frames the same (flicks 49-53); not kept. `chl.tudebug` = sysmem: glass pass 5.0 ms, frame median 13.6, but black wedges at the icons' corners, a broken status-bar clock and a cut Search pill (fetch is wrong in sysmem, as in the earlier round); not kept. **Kept:** memoryless attachments are not stored (Metal never keeps them) and not cleared at the start (chl load action 3 = Vulkan DONT_CARE; contents undefined, as on Apple's tile memory). Measured on one backboardd with the live switch: heavy frames' GPU median 14.7 (off) -> 13.9 (store dropped) -> 13.5 ms (both), p90 18.3 -> 16.0, frames over 12 ms 77 -> 42; per pass: the full-screen `A2Xhf` pass 1.9 -> 1.6 ms, single full-screen draws 0.8 -> 0.6 (no clear of the half-float target in sysmem). Shown frames by `dipper-drag`: unchanged within noise (flicks 48-53). **Why the flick numbers hide it (new, from `kern.sweet_fb_trace`):** the end of each flick runs at 30 fps on purpose (swaps 33 ms apart with scan-out 2 ms after the swap: CoreAnimation's own pacing, nothing late), and `dipper-drag` counts those as 25-34 ms intervals. Counting only real hitches (intervals over 20 ms outside 30 Hz runs, scratch `hitch.py`, 6 flick pairs each, kernel trace after each flick, traces overlap so absolute counts are inflated): on 184 and 252, off 220 and 272 (about 11 % fewer, noisy). Screenshots with it on: home pages, App Library page, Today view and Control Center all clean (rounded icons, clock, Search pill, glass tiles, blur). **Default ON** in the build on the phone; `/private/var/tmp/bgmtl.mloff` restores the old behaviour, `bgmtl.mlstoreonly` drops only the store (both looked at twice a second). **On the phone now:** `/usr/local/lib/bgmtl/libchlorophyll.dylib` 87766fff (rebuilt from mesa-turnip26/build-ios with gpu/metal a5b58cf), `bgmtl-inject.dylib` 9c7c67f1, both in `research/chl-work/out-metal-glass` (built by hand like build-driver.sh); the files before: `/var/root/libchlorophyll.before-glass.dylib` (c66215dc) and `/var/root/bgmtl-inject.before-sched.dylib` (9a3e868f) = `research/chl-work/out-metal`, the confirmed build, still what `ios26-root-chl.simg` holds. **User, by hand (2026-11-07 ~14:24): "Looks clean".** It is now the default build: `research/chl-work/out-metal` holds these files (libchlorophyll 87766fff, inject 9c7c67f1, bgmtl.o, bgmtl_inject.o; the ones before as `*.before-glass`), so the next `renegade update` with `RENEGADE_CHL=1` puts it into the root image (not done: `ios26-root-chl.simg` still has the previous Chlorophyll). Also: `chl.passprof`, `chl.noroa`, `chl.tudebug`, `bgmtl.ml*` removed; backboardd restarted 6 more times (13:58-14:20), healthy each time.
* **WHAT SLOWS THE FLICKS: THE GPU, ON LIQUID GLASS AND FULL-SCREEN HALF-FLOAT PASSES (2026-11-07 13:10-13:56, user: "Yes, profile flicks"; measured, nothing changed on the phone in the end).** Same test as the bullet below (`tools/dipper-drag.sh`, home screen; flicks open the App Library and Today view). **Not the CPU:** `tools/sweetnet/sweetsample` on backboardd during flicks: 37 % of one CPU in all; CoreAnimation renders on its `com.apple.coreanimation.display` threads (the `render-server` thread only waits); with every thread sampled the tick rate falls to 18-30 Hz, too coarse for a per-frame picture. **Not the GPU clock:** `kern.sweet_gpu` polled during flicks: level 7, 710 MHz, boosted, 52-59 % busy while animating (input floor 4 for 300 ms, then the governor). **The heavy frames are GPU-bound:** with `/private/var/tmp/chl.passprof` = `12 0.0` (passes of every frame over 12 ms of GPU, read at backboardd's start), 81-95 frames per two rounds were over 12 ms: median 13.6-15.1 ms, p90 about 17, max about 21, 20-22 passes and 128-144 draws each (App Library and Today view with glass). Where that GPU time goes (passes summed by kind, scratch script): **Liquid Glass passes 47-53 %** (`glass_background_no_bleed`/`_sdf_no_bleed` with `attachment_clear` and the `TimgA2S1Xhfu` composites; one pass alone 3.0-6.2 ms with 33-66 draws), **full-screen 828x1792 passes 28-31 %** (`A2Xhf`/`TimgA2Xhfn_Isrc`: 4 draws in 1.9-2.0 ms, single full-screen draws 0.8 ms each, about the memory bandwidth of half-float (8-byte) pixels), **blur 11-13 %** (downsample, narrow and variable blur), the rest small. Turnip's UBWC compression already applies to CoreAnimation's half-float offscreen textures (usage 5, no storage, not mutable: `ubwc_possible()` in tu_image.cc; no `chl.tudebug`), so it is not a lever. **Tried, no real change:** `CA_DISPLAY_EDR_HEADROOM=1` + `CA_FRAMEBUFFER_EDR_HEADROOM=1` in `/private/var/tmp/bgmtl-bb.env` (the passes stay half-float, `Xhf`; median 13.6 ms, flicks 49-56 = noise); Reduce Transparency on (`sweetprefs mobile com.apple.Accessibility EnhancedBackgroundContrastEnabled bool 1`): the glass shaders still run (glass 50 %), fewer heavy frames (69), flicks 50-56 (0-4 better), then set back (it was int 0, it is now bool false: the same setting). Also: `CA_DISABLE_LUMA_BOOST` is NOT set any more (no env file, nothing in the inject or plists; the luma-boost pass does not show in the heavy frames anyway). The pass lists also show the first flicks after a backboardd restart building pipelines (128 in 335 ms) with 19-30 ms encodes: a restart penalty, gone after one warm-up round. **So:** on iOS 26 the App Library / Today view transitions need about 14-17 ms of A630 time a frame, memory-bound, half of it Liquid Glass; Chlorophyll's CPU side is not the limit. Leads (guesses, not tried): the glass pass's cost under GMEM with framebuffer fetch and raster-order attachment access (chl sets that flag on every fetching pipeline: TURNIP.md), the GMEM/sysmem choice of the single-draw full-screen copies (`chl.autotune`; `prefer_sysmem` was clean and no faster in an earlier round), and whatever CoreAnimation does at a lower backdrop resolution (`CA_BACKDROP_SCALE` exists, semantics unknown). Phone state after: `chl.passprof`, `bgmtl-bb.env`, test files removed, inject 9a3e868f, backboardd restarted eight times today between 13:00 and 13:55 (each time healthy, home screen after `sweetundim unlock`). CoreAnimation's environment variable names (394) are in QuartzCore's strings: `DSC_DIR=research/ios26/dsc python3 tools/renegade/dsctools/imgstr.py QuartzCore CA_` (without `-I`: it imports its sibling symb.py).
* **DEFERRED RECORDING THREAD (HakiOS's `metal_defer` idea) FOR CHLOROPHYLL: MEASURED, NOT BUILT: IT CANNOT HELP (2026-11-07 12:45-13:07, user: "Yes, try it"; phone on image 118, nothing left changed).** **Baseline, confirmed build (inject 9a3e868f), `tools/dipper-drag.sh`, home screen (one page, plain blue wallpaper; screenshot checked):** drags 53.1-60.0 fps shown, flicks 47.6-55.5 (flicks: 25-34 ms intervals in 15-25% of frames); 97-100% of rendered frames shown. **bgmtl.perf (per command buffer):** drags (60 cbuf/s, ~80 draws) encode 1.0-1.4 ms, submit ~0.2, GPU 3.3-4.4; the heavy seconds of the flicks (44-62 cbuf/s, 79-92 draws) encode 2.3-6.5 ms, submit 0.2-0.9, GPU 8-14 ms with peaks 21-38 ms. **bgmtl.encprof (backboardd restarted with it, then off again):** all of Chlorophyll's chl_* calls together are about 0.46 ms a frame on drags and 0.65-0.95 ms in the heavy seconds; the render thread's whole CPU per frame (`frame-cpu`, commit to commit) is 3.3-4.0 ms on drags and 5.2-9.5 ms in the heavy seconds, out of 16.7. So moving chl's recording to its own thread would take under 1 ms off a thread that is idle most of each frame: no gain to expect, not built. (HakiOS needed it because its plug-in costs about 40 us a draw on the render thread; ours costs about 5-11.) **Also disproved on the way:** the idea that backboardd's frames are serialized behind the GPU because `waitUntilScheduled` waits for completion in the compositor (bgmtl.m since 4762d9d, while the scheduled handlers went back to "submitted" in d1d04a6): a test build counting the waits (and a live switch making waitUntilScheduled return at submit) showed CoreAnimation calls NEITHER waitUntilScheduled NOR waitUntilCompleted in backboardd (0 calls in every second over two rounds), and the switch changed nothing (drags 54-60, flicks 48-54 either way). The test build is gone (gpu/metal source reverted, `research/chl-work/out-metal-sched` deleted), the confirmed inject is back (`/usr/local/lib/bgmtl/bgmtl-inject.dylib` = 9a3e868f; the copy taken before, `/var/root/bgmtl-inject.before-sched.dylib`, is the same file), `bgmtl.encprof` removed, backboardd restarted three times between 13:00 and 13:07 and healthy each time. **What does limit the flicks (open):** neither Chlorophyll's encode nor the render thread's CPU; the GPU's 8-14 ms per heavy frame with 21-38 ms peaks, plus whatever backboardd's render thread waits on in the other ~10 ms of each frame (not read). Next measurements if wanted: a thread sample of backboardd during flicks (as `research/chl-work/bbwait-1.txt` once did) and `/private/var/tmp/chl.passprof` for which passes take the GPU time. **Test tool:** `/var/root/sweetundim` on the phone is the old wake/unlock tool (`git show 238f4d0:tools/sweetnet/sweetwake.c`, rebuilt with the sweettouch recipe: arm64e, touch.entitlements, pacstrip --sign; `sweetundim unlock` wakes and unlocks); today's `tools/sweetnet/sweetwake.c` with the same name is the timer-latency tool, so the screen could not be woken over SSH without it.
* **NATIVE METAL PATH (HakiOS's hakios-metal) FOR CHLOROPHYLL: FEASIBILITY, READ-ONLY (2026-11-07 12:15-12:40, user: "yeah check the feasibility of native metal path"; hakios-xnu-kernel @ 63fc2b4 sparse-cloned into the scratchpad, nothing built or run, nothing copied).** **Verdict: not worth a port now; take two of its ideas instead.**
  **What hakios-metal is (observed in its source and docs):** a C++ library, MIT (`hakios-metal/LICENSE`; the GPU numbers are Mesa's, MIT, per its NOTICE), about 7k lines of headers plus `src/` (render.cpp 3353, compiler.cpp 1663, c_api.cpp 1645, texture.cpp 1324, compute.cpp 680, command.cpp 676), that writes the Adreno's PM4 packets itself (registers after Turnip's and fd6's sequences), compiles AIR -> NIR (their front end) -> ir3 (Mesa) in-process, draws into IOSurfaces directly, has its own GMEM/sysmem autotune per pass, and talks msm-DRM requests to their kernel plus two of its own (0x7e buffer over an IOSurface ID, 0x7d userptr). Its C API (`hakios_metal.h`) is what their window-server plug-in calls. That plug-in, `userland/src/HakiosMetalCA.m` (8747 lines), is "begun from vcvkk's ... that repository states no license" (their THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES: **to verify**), so it is not usable by us; the library is. It is built for ONE chip: `kChipId = 0x06030500` (Adreno 7c+ Gen 3 / 642L family, A6xx gen 4), `kGmemBytes = 512 KB`, CCU offsets and "num_ccu 2, fibers" from Mesa's row for that chip; nobody has run it on an A630 (the OnePlus 6T fork draws through OpenGL ES, not Metal). Still refused by name (its source, today): multisampling, stencil, textures chosen at run time, several mip/slice/3D cases, sample masks; its README lists 2D-only one-level textures and no threadgroup memory as of late October.
  **Why HakiOS's "2x" does not carry over to us:** the slow path it beat on the same phone, metal2vulkan (UniXNU's AdrenoMetal + steelbrain/metal2vulkan, AIR -> SPIR-V -> Turnip), renders each frame into a tiled image and merges it back into the IOSurface with a compute pass, and goes through SPIR-V (their docs/reference/metal-measurements.md: GPU 14-21 ms a frame vs about 10 for hakios-metal). Chlorophyll does neither: AIR -> NIR straight into Turnip through its own in-process runtime `chl` (no SPIR-V, no loader; docs/TURNIP.md), and the IOSurface imported as a linear DRM-modifier image and rendered into directly (`chl_texture_from_iosurface`, air/chl_vk.c), with Turnip's GMEM/sysmem autotune (`/private/var/tmp/chl.autotune`). CPU per draw is already no worse: chl's 200-draw bench 5.0-7.5 us/draw (TURNIP.md) vs hakios-metal's 200 draws in 2.6 ms first call to last pixel, 0.42 ms of it GPU (about 11 us/draw, their README). The luma-boost pass they drop we already drop (CA_DISABLE_LUMA_BOOST, GPU 12 -> 10.6 ms on unlock, SMOOTHNESS round). And they run iOS 16.5 (no Liquid Glass) on a 120 Hz panel; we run iOS 26.6.2 on a 60 Hz one, so at most about 49-53 -> 60 fps on heavy pages is on the table.
  **What a port would take (estimate, guess):** retarget to the A630 (chip id 0x06030001, GMEM 1 MB, CCU offsets, Turnip's a630 init/"magic" registers, then bisect boots with GPU-hang recovery: one to two weeks); a transport onto our kernel's GPU driver (its msm requests + the IOSurface/userptr ones; we have SURFACE_BO: days); an adapter implementing `air/chl.h` (274 lines) over `hakios_metal.h` so `src/bgmtl.m` stays as it is (one to two weeks); then everything iOS 26's CoreAnimation, Mercury and RenderBox use that chl already serves and hakios-metal refuses: 4x MSAA resolves, stencil, run-time texture/level choice (Mercury's level slots), mip levels and views, threadgroup memory, ASTC, XR10 two-plane and YCbCr, RGBA16F glass passes (weeks to months). Expected GPU gain over Turnip: unknown, likely none (Turnip's register streams are mature, and our remaining time is CoreAnimation's own encode plus about 10 ms of GPU); a regression risk on every feature.
  **Cheaper ideas from HakiOS worth trying first (their measurements, not ours):** (1) `metal_defer=1`: the window server's command buffers recorded on a thread of the driver's own, so a draw costs the render thread about 5 us instead of about 40 (their plug-in). For us: chl recording is about 2.3 ms of backboardd's 4.6 ms encode (170 draws, 47 passes, SMOOTHNESS round 3); moving it off the render thread could take that off the frame's critical path. (2) `wallpaper_freeze=1`: the wallpaper as one still picture in SpringBoard (read from the IOSurface on the panel), with `metal_defer` home button 50 -> 89-92 fps there; iOS 26's poster wallpaper likely costs us GPU time every frame too (guess, not measured). Both need our own implementation (their plug-in's code is the unlicensed part; the idea is free).
* **MODEM AND SIM: WHAT OTHER PROJECTS HAVE, AND OUR SLOTS READ OUT (2026-11-07 11:35-12:05, user: "check first of all, modem and sim status on other projects and forks, update our findings"; read-only, nothing sent to the network, no SIM in the phone).**
  **Our phone (observed, image 118 / xnu 3072d; the 3057 QMI pass-through is also in the default image 109):** DMS Get Operating Mode (0x2d) still 5 = "shutting down", with no offline-reason (TLV 0x10) or hardware-restricted (0x11) TLV. **UIM Get Slot Status (0x47): both physical slots "card absent", both slots active, physical 1 -> logical 1, physical 2 -> logical 2, no ATR, not eUICC.** So Get Card Status's "card 0/1 error, code 3 (no ATR)" is what an empty slot looks like on this modem (HakiOS saw the same code on its empty slot while the other slot read the SIM): nothing points at a SIM-interface fault. The modem announces its IPA QMI service (0x31 instance 2), DPM (0x2f) and WDA (0x1a); nothing on our side talks to them. Our SMP2P outbound item to the modem has the `ipa` entry (beryllium_wlan.c `ms_smp2p_out_setup`), value 0 (no bit set).
  **HakiOS (oosexgang/hakios-xnu-kernel, POCO X5 Pro SM7325, iOS 16.5 userland; docs/cellular.md and the run diary docs/ru/cellular.md, last modem news late October; MIT/APSL; read, nothing copied): kernel-only cellular, no CommCenter.** In order: (1) the modem stays OFFLINE and refuses ONLINE ("device not ready", 52) until the AP serves TFTP and the service-registry locator (we already serve both); (2) after ONLINE it crashed within seconds in `enl2_dl` (LTE L2 downlink) until the AP side of the IPA existed: IPA firmware through TZ and its RPMh clock vote, SMMU streams, SMEM item 497 (`SMEM_IPA_FILTER_TABLE`, 0x9000), the IPA QMI INIT_DRIVER handshake (service 0x31), and the deciding piece, the SMP2P `ipa` entry set to 3 (bit 0 valid, bit 1 clock on): without it the modem's IPA task waits forever (`IPA_SMP2P: Could not wait for inbound SMP2P channel readiness`); (3) SIM: card status "slot 1 ERROR code 3 (empty), slot 2 PRESENT, USIM READY", the primary subscription on empty logical slot 1 -> UIM Switch Slot (0x46) logical 1 -> physical 2, then UIM Change Provisioning Session (0x38: primary GW, activate, slot 1 + the USIM AID; also for a USIM that is only "detected"), then NAS Initiate Network Register; (4) signal -70...-87 dBm on UMTS, then "full LTE service" (cellular.md; their docs/index.md table still says "no registration yet"); data (DPM Open Port -> WDA raw IP/QMAP -> WDS Bind Mux -> Start Network Interface, a fake Ethernet `en1` with kernel ARP/DHCP) not working yet; no calls, no SMS; signal bars through a SpringBoard hook.

How: in cpu_idle, instead of WFI, PSCI CPU_SUSPEND (0xC4000001) with power_state 0x40000004 (rail-pc; 0x40000003 = pc) and `sweet_secondary_entry` as the entry; the core returns through the reset vector -> cpu_reset_handler = resume_idle_cpu (set by cpu_machine_idle_init) -> start_cpu -> arm_init_idle_cpu, where `sweet_deep_idle_resume` redoes the GIC CPU interface (PE_init_cpu) and re-arms the timer, -> cpu_idle_exit(TRUE) -> Idle_load_context. Data the reset path reads with the MMU off is cleaned to PoC once per CPU (same list as cpu_start). CPU 0 never powers down and is the sleepers' timer: a sleeper publishes its pop minus 1.1 ms, sends CPU 0 SIGPTimerLocal if that is earlier than CPU 0's rtcPop; CPU 0 adds the earliest to its decrementer (end of timer_resync_deadlines) and sends a nop IPI when it passes (start of timer_intr); store/fence/load on both sides. Live: `kern.sweet_deep_idle` (0 off = boot default, 1 rail-pc, 2 pc), `_mask` (0xFE), `_screen` (1 = only while iOS has the display off, the default), `_min_us` 3000, `_lead_us` 1100, `_stats`. **Observed:** CPU 1 alone 10 s: 1906 power-downs, 1906 resumes, 0 returns/errors, down 57% of the time; CPUs 1-7 30 s: each down 58-90% of the time, no errors, SpringBoard/backboardd kept their processes; worst wake after a core's own timer 4.8 ms (cpu5, once; 954 us cpu2; others 0): probably CPU 0 busy with interrupts masked (guess). **A/B, screen off (`sweettouch lock`), cable cut by `kern.sweet_usbin_off=45`, 32 samples a window, medians, order 0 1 2 0 1 2: off 155 / 138.5, rail-pc 132 / 121, pc 141 / 118.5 mA** (script research/chl-work/deepidle/ab4.sh). * **LOST KEYBOARD TAPS FIXED (xnu 3051 + 3052). DEFAULT BOOT IS NOW IMAGE 78: `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-78-touchdrain.img` (sha256 135050d117d11502..., xnu 3001-3052 `--remake`, kernel `.3052` sha256 e124f63cbfd1fd4e..., research tree 7a10c08 + 5334591, `xnu/patches-12377/3051-touch-identity.patch`, `3052-dipper-touch-drain.patch`; `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh` reproduces it byte for byte) (user 2026-11-05: removed the widgets himself, "homescreen feels better", Spotlight typing fine, but "apps feels laggy ... settings scrolling is heavy, same applies to notes and typing in it, ui heavy and losing taps on keyboard").** **Measured with the user's finger:** touch rate is fine: a continuous drag gives 10-19 events per 100 ms (~125/s; my first '32/s' was an average with the finger lifted, wrong). Settings (SwiftUI) scrolling: Settings 58-66% of one core (main thread: CoreAnimation commits ~40%, SwiftUI view graph ~26%), backboardd 37%, frames 57-60 fps (127 intervals, median 16.7 ms): Apple's per-frame work on an A75 at full clock; 'heavy' is most likely latency, not dropped frames (not measured: needs a touch->scan marker). **Taps:** 30 fast taps in Notes, 30 ENTER events in the kernel (kern.sweet_touch_stats downs, sampled every 200 ms by a script started before typing), 24 letters, twice; after 3051 alone ~20 letters, and a screenshot showed the 'a' key popup still up with no finger on the glass, `active=0x1` in the kernel. **Cause (3052):** touch_stfts drained the FIFO and reported once at the end, so a LEAVE and the next ENTER of the same slot read in one drain cancelled out: iOS saw the old finger slide to the new key and never lift. The drain also stopped when the IRQ line read high after a read (3007), which can leave the LEAVE queued until the next touch brings it in with that touch's ENTER. Now lifts and touch-downs are reported as read (motions once per drain), the FIFO is read until NO EVENT (one empty read per drain), and an ENTER on a held slot lifts the old contact first (`stale=` counter: 0 in the test, so the collapsing was the whole story). **3051:** every new contact gets a new HID identity (was slot + 2), as Apple's driver does; kept, but on its own it did not help. **Result (user, boot 78): "All 30 appeared"**, kernel downs = taps, stale 0, active back to 0 after the lift. Tools: /var/root/touchrate (touch counters every 100 ms), /tmp/tapmon.sh pattern (counter started before the user types).

* **THE SPEAKER'S GUARD REPLACES THE -12 dB CEILING (user 2026-11-05: "Yes, build the guard"; commit 3b02ce0). `tools/audio/SweetSpeaker/guard.c` (+ guard.h, Mac test guard_test.c), our own code after HakiOS's design (docs/FORKS_SURVEY.md G9), in SweetSpeaker.driver after the volume control:** +12 dB make-up (VirtualAudio runs Apple's `n104_speaker_general` chain on our port: pre-gain -10.7 to -14 dB, observed in audiomxd's log), 2nd-order Butterworth high-pass at 200 Hz, power limits over 0.2 / 3 / 60 s at -3 / -6 / -9 dB under a full-scale sine (the gain is the largest that keeps every average of the power reaching the speaker at or under its limit, from the power smoothed over 10 ms; drops at once, recovers over 100 ms; the averages decay through IO pauses, guard_rest at StartIO), peak limiter at -3 dBFS (43 ms release). **Reference level:** the amp stays at DAC gain 2; Android's programs run it at 15 (scan of tas2557_uCDSP_*.bin: Tuning Mode and ROM Mode 1 both write SPK_CTRL 0x7c, calibration 0x34 = 6; the dB per step is not in TI's driver), and the guard treats gain 2 as if it were the loudest: stricter than HakiOS at Android's level. **Mac test, observed:** a -12 dBFS 1 kHz tone (= Apple's chain at full scale) for 70 s comes out at -3 dB for ~3 s, -6 dB to ~40 s, -9 dB after 60 s, all three averages at or under their limits, peaks never over -3 dBFS, lowest gain -9 dB (an earlier version fed the averages the instantaneous power and dipped to silence: fixed); -32 dBFS only lifted 12 dB; high-pass within 0.05 dB of Butterworth at 50/100/200/400/1000 Hz. **On the phone (driver sha256 91e667451b98ed7f, installed live, audiomxd restarted):** silence and tones 0 gaps/skips; the user stepped -40 -> -30 -> -20 dBFS (sweetaq 440 Hz): clean at every step, amp flags 0x02/0x00, the guard took 0.0 dB off (not loud enough to reach its limits), **user: "Clean, good level"**. * **iOS PLAYS THROUGH THE SPEAKER: SweetSpeaker.driver (user 2026-11-04: "Yes, start it", the iOS audio device). xnu 3046 (research tree cbcd979, `xnu/patches-12377/3046-dipper-audio-play-anybody.patch`, kernel `.3046` sha256 3568f0fe86ca82e2..., image `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-70-hal.img` = sweetaudio=3): kern.sweet_audio_play CTLFLAG_ANYBODY (audiomxd runs as mobile), pl_status.done_time.** **How iOS 26 picks the speaker (observed, audiomxd's unified log + VirtualAudio disassembly):** audiomxd loads AudioServerPlugIn drivers (type 443ABAB8-...) from `/System/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL/*.driver` (AirPlay, CarPlay, BT, TimeSync, Apple's BuiltinAudioPlugin, which needs IOPAudio* kernel services we do not have); VirtualAudio's DeviceFactory (HALDeviceManager.cpp, text+0xe1294..) builds its device classes BY DEVICE UID: Codec, Baseband Voice, USB Audio Output, USB IDAM, **Speaker**, AppleSongbirdDSP, PuffinInput/Output, Actuator, AOP Audio-1, HP16Mic, Digital Mic, DigitalMic, Mic, Hawking, Flicker, Penrose, Halogen, ..., Receiver, LPMicInjection; anything else ("Null_Device") is "Unhandled UID" and gets null ports only. **New `tools/audio/SweetSpeaker/` (SweetSpeaker.c, Info.plist, build.sh -> research/sweetnet/ios18/SweetSpeaker.driver, arm64e, pacstrip, ad-hoc):** one output device UID "Speaker", 2 ch Float32 48 kHz, volume + mute controls, transport built-in; WriteMix -> 16-bit -> kern.sweet_audio_play DATA; gain ceiling -12 dB (ROM mode, no speaker protection); host clock at 400 ticks/frame; a helper thread restarts the kernel player when it was not up at StartIO; logs under com.sweet.SweetSpeaker (`sweetlog 60 SweetSpeaker`: per-run skips/overlaps/ring gaps). Installed live on the phone in /System/Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/HAL (root:wheel; copy with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar --uid 0 --gid 0` or macOS adds `._*` files), NOT in the root build yet. Result: VirtualAudio `Adding port [ type: pspk; uid: Speaker ]` (+ pspr Speaker Telemetry, pstp Speaker Tap Stream Input), AudioQueues route to it, StartIO/StopIO follow the clients. **The breaks (user: "Broken up") were the 24 MHz clock:** the HAL computed 500 host ticks/frame (`AudioGetHostClockFrequency` 24e6, cycle info mDeviceHostTicksPerFrame 500), so every zero time stamp read as "host time is not consecutive": re-anchoring + overload about every 0.4 s and 16 skips (0.92 s) in 9 s. **Fix: `tools/renegade/timebase_cache.py` applied to the phone's cache (user OK "Yes, patch and reboot")**: 13 audio images in 8 sub-caches (.05 .19 .23 .31 .40 .50 .73 .75; originals kept as `*.orig` in /System/Library/Caches/com.apple.dyld), boot 70b fine, `AudioGetHostClockFrequency` 19200000, HAL 400 ticks/frame, 0 overloads. NOT in the root build yet (root_tweaks18 should run it; the script header still says "not used"). User then heard "One small click" (1 kernel gap at the AudioQueue's start); prefill raised 2400 -> 4800 frames: next run 94 cycles, 0 skips, 0 gaps, ring never below 19200 B; replayed (96 cycles, 0 skips, 0 gaps): **user: "Steady tone"** (no breaks, no clicks), 2026-11-04 ~17:28 CET. **Pitfalls:** at boot something holds the device's IO open (the stream then runs for hours with zeros: 2.7 h, 1.85 GB, 0 gaps) and the kernel player starts before `dipper-speaker.sh amp-register`, which then fails EBUSY: stop, register, stop (`sweetplay -x; sp.sh amp-register; sweetplay -x`). **Next:** amp scripts registrable while playing + a root job registering them at boot; amp off after seconds of silence; the driver and the cache patch into the root build; then real content (Safari/YouTube) and the volume buttons.

DEFAULT BOOT IS NOW `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-37-full.img` (xnu 3001-3019, built from scratch on this Mac, see the next bullet).** **3017, panel:** the EA8074 sets its own brightness (DCS 0x51, 10 bits, big endian: Linux `mipi_dsi_dcs_set_display_brightness_ss`; WLED MOD_EN reads 0). The kernel sends it through the DSI host's FIFO as `dsi_ctrl_hw_cmn_kickoff_fifo_command` does (TPG custom pattern FIFO, words 0xc0390003 and 0xff|lo|hi|0x51, LP mode, length 8, software trigger; DSI0 at 0x0ae94000). The vsync timer starts a send and looks for DMA_DONE on a later tick, it never spins. `kern.sweet_fb_bl=2..1023` sets it by hand (0 = iOS decides), `kern.sweet_fb_bl_now` reads the last level sent. * **NEWS OPENS: FairPlay's Mach services never answered, and that blocked locationd and every CoreLocation client.** Observed: News' main thread in `objc_sync_enter` under `-[CLLocationManager onClientEventRegistration:]`, the lock held by a NewsFeed thread in a synchronous XPC call to locationd (`getAuthorizationStatus:`), locationd stuck in two places. **(1) ARI:** a silo thread in `ice::Client::start` -> `Ari::AriClientXpc::registerClient`, semaphore wait for ever: the non-cellular CommCenter job advertises `com.apple.commcenter.ari.rt.xpc` and did not answer in any sample. Taking the name out of the job's MachServices made that wait go away (0 libARI/libICEClient frames on the next boot). News still hung. **(2) FairPlay:** a locationd thread in a raw MIG call, id 1203. Method: a one-off tool read the message's remote port from the stuck frame (task_for_pid, FP walk), copied the right, and compared it with `bootstrap_look_up` of all 2351 names in launchd.plist: it IS `com.apple.fairplayd.versioned`, job `com.apple.fairplayd.H2`. `fairplayd.H2` run by hand exits at once with status 0 and no message; under launchd it was exec'd 6 times in 5.5 min (KeepAlive, ThrottleInterval 60) and was not running when sampled. Why it exits is a guess (no FairPlay hardware), not looked into. launchd keeps the names, so requests sit in the queue for ever. **Fix:** `tools/sweetnet/sweetfpd.c` takes the job (`Program` in launchd.plist; `root_tweaks18.py` FAIRPLAY_JOB, in `tools/sweetnet/build.sh`): checks in the job's 4 names, answers MIG requests with MIG_BAD_ID, destroys anything else, logs the first 64 to `/private/var/tmp/sweetfpd.log`. **Result (boot 29c):** the log shows 24 requests in the first 2 minutes from 10 different processes (ids 1200, 1202, 1203; one non-MIG id), so far more than locationd was waiting on it; locationd has no thread at the FairPlay call. News shows "Welcome to Apple News" with its main thread idle in the run loop (research/shots/dipper-apps-after-fpd.png has the other apps). Reminders opens with its iCloud alert. **Still blank, main thread not sampled this time:** App Store (white), Games and Music (black): likely network or account, a guess; no Wi-Fi network is joined. Health was not tested (the phone had locked). New on that boot, one each, not looked at: healthd SIGSEGV at 0x0 (does not recur so far), tccd and managedappdistributiond killed by jetsam (ns 1 code 7). **Live on the phone:** `/usr/local/bin/sweetfpd`, `/System/Library/xpc/launchd.plist` = `/var/root/launchd.plist.fp` (previous: `.noari`, `.bt`). `research/ios26/ios26-root-chl.simg` was rebuilt at 23:54 BEFORE this fix: rebuild it again, nothing flashed. Pitfall: a launchd job whose Program is missing at boot stays down for that boot even with KeepAlive; put the binary there first.

DEFAULT BOOT IS NOW `research/ios26/enxerto-boot-dipper-ios26-28-arm64e.img`** (fork CI run 41137319497, errors.txt empty, kernel sha256 ec5bb0c76705a133..., `xnu/out-dipper-41137319497/`, xnu 3001-3013, args of `tools/dipper-mkboot.sh`). **3012, arm64e:** `host_info` answers CPU_SUBTYPE_ARM64E under `sweetarm64e=1`. Test: override removed and the MobileGestalt cache deleted before the boot; the cache came back by itself (9675 B), MGCopyAnswer("arm64e") = 1, `hw.cpusubtype` = 2, 42 modules loadable, Control Center complete. So the guess was right and a fresh image needs no override. Copy with the override in /var/root/MobileGestalt.with-override.plist, not in use. **3013, false PMIC readings.** Symptoms: iOS told 100%/4200 mV/full for a poll (Control Center's 100%, sweetmetrics flipping 70% <-> 100%), `typec_rp` 0 for one read, a fake unplug, a fake temperature fault, each costing about a minute at 500 mA (9 restores in 40 min; 27% of samples at 423 mA). **Observed cause:** SPMI observer reads come back with an error bit now and then: `SWEET SPMI: read sid=2 addr=0x1042 status 0x9, try 0` (5 in the first 3.5 min, always try 0, so the first retry worked). Why the bus fails them is not known. **Fix:** sweet_spmi_read retries up to 3 times (first 16 errors logged); pollBeryllium keeps the last good measurement (100% only if there never was one) and accepts FG words within 64 counts (voltage noise made equal reads rare); unplug and fault need 2 ticks in a row (3 s) while applied; an Rp change only restarts when the limit would change. **Seen so far (boot 28, 3.5 min):** 85% 4273 mV +932 mA charging, `restores=1`. **Battery today:** 45% -> 85% in 90 min of this testing. Not rechecked at length: see below if the restore count stays low.
* **SAFARI OPENS: apps needing a data container had none on record.** A visual sweep of the 16 home-screen apps: most fine, Safari aborted 130-160 ms after launch: `Safari received a nil container URL from LSApplicationRecord which must not happen unless Safari has been deleted`, then `-[NSURL initFileURLWithPath:isDirectory:]: nil string parameter` (run from SSH it prints the reason; the .ips only says abort). **Cause:** `sweetuicache` gave extensions their container, entitlements and group containers but not the app itself. `LSApplicationRecord.dataContainerURL` nil, `isContainerized` 0 (research/chl-work/lsq.m). **Fix:** tools/sweetnet/sweetuicache.m: `Entitlements` and `GroupContainers` for the app too; with `com.apple.private.security.container-required` (true or a string) also `Container` (MCMAppDataContainer), `EnvironmentVariables` (HOME, CFFIXED_USER_HOME, TMPDIR) and **`IsContainerized`**: without that last key LaunchServices ignores the rest (seen: Container alone left the record nil). Live: all of /Applications re-registered: 254 ok, 88 containerized, 201 s, 2 without a bundle id (RepairCal + one more, not looked at); backup /var/root/sweetuicache.before-containers. **Result:** Safari stays up and shows its Start Page (research/shots/dipper-safari.png), 0 `nil container` after that. **Side effect:** those 88 apps now have HOME in their container, so app data that was in /var/mobile before (first-run state) is not seen; nothing of value was there on this phone. **Still open from the same sweep:** Maps, News, Games and App Store showed a black or white page after 4.5-5.5 s, not yet understood (no crash; no network joined; the sweep was partly cut by auto-lock). The first-boot job already calls sweetuicache for every app, so a rebuilt image gets this. **Also (small):** time zone on the phone: `/var/db/timezone/localtime` -> Europe/Amsterdam (was US/Pacific, the root's default), the Mac's zone; lock screen shows it. Only on this phone, not in the image.
